- The `fgos run` and `fgos workflow` help say which door to use: one task → `fgos run "<prompt>"`; planned work → `fgos workflow start <preset>|--units <file>`.
- A fresh checkout, a linked worktree and `fgos setup` no longer need `npm install`: fgOS has no npm runtime dependency now. Its YAML parser (js-yaml) ships inside the source tree and every YAML read goes through one wrapper, `src/util/yaml.mjs`, so `fgos doctor` check `dependencies-installed` passes with "no runtime dependencies declared" and the workflow tests load without `node_modules`.
- Agent definitions (`fgos/agents`, `domains/*/agents`, `core/agents`) and project or domain workflow files must be valid YAML. `fgos doctor` names a file that is not, with its line and column, in the checks `agent-claims-resolve`, `agent-type-names-unique`, `workflow-capabilities-configured`, `workflow-pools-satisfy-independence` and `blind-steps-use-proven-pools`; a seat that names such a definition is refused, and the agent roster skips it with one warning line on stderr. A definition indented as a whole now reads as a mapping and seats; a numeric `name: 123` reads as "123".
- `fgos doctor` checks `workflow-pools-satisfy-independence` and `blind-steps-use-proven-pools` now evaluate in a copy without dependencies instead of passing with "not evaluated", so a project can see new failures there. A workflow that cannot be parsed fails those checks and `workflow-capabilities-configured` by name, but no longer hides their results for the other workflows. A problem path is prefixed `package:` or `project:` when both trees are scanned, and a file that cannot be read is reported as such rather than as unparsable.
- A persona whose list item or value reads as a mapping (an unquoted `": "`, for example `- Escalate when: budget exceeded`) is refused with its path by `fgos agents`, `fgos doctor` and persona resolution, instead of the text being dropped silently. Pinned text from an earlier run with that shape still renders as it was pinned.
- A workspace persona that cannot be parsed or has the wrong shape refuses `fgos run` and workflow unit runs with the named problem; before, the run fell back to the core persona of the same name or to no persona text.
- A YAML file whose aliases expand past 100000 values, or that references itself, is rejected with a message naming the file.
- `fgos doctor` check `agent-type-names-unique` reports problems as `<file>: <problem>`, like the other checks. The dispatch warning `agent roster: …` for a bad agent file prints once per process instead of on every lookup.
- `fgos doctor` check `domain-registry-compiled` now also reports a `compiled.json` that is stale against its YAML and domain YAML that cannot be parsed; `npm run build:domains` regenerates it.
- Persona text rendered into a worker prompt now comes from the parsed agent file: a block-scalar value shows in full, an inline `# comment` is stripped and a number is normalised (`1e3` shows as `1000`). A persona file that cannot be parsed renders one `could not be parsed` line instead of silently dropping its section; a run pinned by an earlier release resumes with the persona text it was pinned with.
- The doctor check for orphaned confinement resources skips attempt homes (they belong to adopt) and its fix goes through the same sweep as the other cleanup call sites; it never removes an attempt home.

### Removed
- The controller's herdr round: the polling loop, its deadline and idle handling, the settle and pane-closing code, the launcher script and its process checks, `herdr-reconcile`, the liveness probe and `herdr-diagnosis.json`, and the pane, endpoint and launch-time fields of the home ownership marker. A home written with a pane binding by an older release is no longer swept: clean it with that release before activating this one.

- The Node run supervisor (`detached-run-supervisor.mjs`), its IPC channel to the controller and its pane-less home binding (`bindConfinedHomesToSupervisor`), the old cli-spawn reconciler (`reconcile-cli-spawn.mjs`), the `legacySpawn` option and the `protected/supervisor-binding` and `protected/adapter-receipts` files of cli-spawn runs. Runs started before this release keep their files and are read as `legacy-run`.
- `fgos doctor` check `provider-capacity-lock-stale`: the provider-capacity state is no longer guarded by a lock file a dead process can leave behind.
- `fgos-runner --config <path>`: the runner and its workers always use the repo's own `.fgos/config.json`.
- `fgos dispatch execute` is gone, together with its `--contract` and `--assignment` forms and the `node src/runner/dispatch.mjs execute` alias. Run one task with `fgos run "<prompt>" --provider <executor>` (`--provider` takes an agent executor; a `kind: "tool"` executor is called directly) (add `--writes <paths> --worktree <linked-worktree>` for work that changes files; the runner commits them), or a Unit file with `fgos run --unit <file>`; planned work goes through `fgos workflow start`. Calling the old door returns an error naming the replacement, and the dispatch-decide hook's BLOCKED message names the same `fgos run` form.
- `fgos dispatch log` is gone: every `fgos run` already records its Unit, binding, results and commit under `.fgos/assignments/<unitRunId>/`.
- `dispatch fanout-batch` is gone. Fanout runs from `node src/runner/fanout-batch.mjs "<ids>" [--has-live-task-access]`, with the same output keys (`fired`, `mechanismChanged`, `unavailable`, `deferred`, and `slotsFull: true` when no slot is free).
- `decide --work` runs only as `fgos dispatch decide --work <id>`; `node src/runner/dispatch.mjs decide --work` is refused with a pointer to it.
- `AGENTS.md` and every skill render no longer teach the removed doors. Other projects keep their old rendered skills until they activate a release that carries this change and run `fgos setup`.
- The `yaml` npm dependency, the hand-written YAML readers in the doctor checks and the persona renderer, and the "not evaluated: yaml package not installed" branches. `fgos doctor` no longer warns about multi-line persona markers because they now render.

### Fixed
- `fgos dispatch recover` no longer parks an orphaned attempt only because `outbox/result-N.json` exists, and a unit whose only attempt the legacy sweep settled no longer reads `running`.
- Attempts left `running` with no holder are cleaned up: new ones through adopt (`run-attempts-stuck`), runs from before the run supervisor through `legacy-attempts-stuck`.
- The gate of a supervised attempt can read its envelope and run when the run directory or the host binary lives under `/tmp`: the sandbox mounts its own `/tmp`, so both are now bound back in place. Before, such a run ended `gate-lost` with `envelope unreadable`.
- A `FGOS_HOST_BIN` that names a file that cannot be run is now an error everywhere the host is looked up; it no longer falls back to the activated release.
- A borrowed lock no longer kills unrelated child processes of the lock holder: cleanup kills the borrowed command, its process group and any escaped descendant that still holds the lock, and waits for the holder’s other children that are between fork and exec (Rust and Node use the same rule). A borrow also refuses a lock whose file was replaced (`lock-resource-replaced`).
- Process containment no longer reports `spawn-failed` when a short command exits before its identity is read; a gate that already exited counts as an empty domain.
- A gemini worker now runs the model its tier asks for. Since gemini moved to omp, the omp invocations passed no `--model`, so every tier ran the profile default (`gemini-3.8-flash`); a frontier task now runs `gemini-4-argon`.
- `fgos take`, `fgos list` and every other verb that reads active claims no longer spawn one git process per open claim; with 60 open claims a `take` drops from about 270 child processes and 1.7 s to 21 processes and 0.26 s.

- The advance and recovery locks no longer stay stuck when their holder dies while creating the lock file; both now live under the run's `locks/` directory.
- The `fgos run --resume` guard no longer treats a dispatch lock it cannot read as free.
- `fgos dispatch reconcile` help, usage errors and docs no longer advertise the retired `clear-assignment-claim` action (and its `--assignment` flag); the planner already refused it, so the supported actions are `clear-cwd-lock`, `collect-result` and `repair-projection`.
- The confinement orphan reaper no longer deletes the private home (and the login copy in it) of a worker that is still running when the process that launched it dies. A confined herdr round now records its pane, the herdr socket its client used, its own pid and start time and the time of binding in the home's ownership marker before the worker starts (a round that cannot record this closes its pane and fails), and a cli-spawn round records its detached run supervisor the same way. A home whose recorded process is alive is kept for its run timeout plus launch and settle grace from that moment, whatever herdr answers; a home bound to a pane that never received a worker is removed and the empty pane closed. Panes of default-session rounds can now be asked about, and the reaper re-reads the marker before removing a home, skipping one that changed since it decided.
- `fgos run --provider <executor>` (a bare executor id in a Unit's `prefer`) inside herdr now binds the executor's herdr invocation, as a capability pool does, instead of the confined cli invocation posture approval had filled in (transport source `unit-prefer-pinned-invocation`). A `prefer` entry that names an invocation, or an override's invocation, still keeps it.
- Releasing another writer's runtime claim is now auditable after the claim file is gone: `fgos unclaim` appends a `decision` event (`source: unclaim`, `kind: engine`) with `admin: {reason, ownerWriterId, releasedByWriterId, claimId}`, and the stale-claim reclaim in `pick` adds the same `admin` field to the decision it already wrote. A writer releasing its own claim records nothing new.
- `fgos run --rigor low` (and a Unit's `rigor: low`) now binds the nano tier when the capability declares no `rigor` floor; bind used to treat the implicit `standard` as a floor, so a low run on `execute` resolved `sonnet` instead of the `nano` model. A capability's own `rigor` still raises a lower Unit rigor.
- `/fgOS:terminal` and `/fgOS:terminal-close` act only on the caller's own live herdr pane. Before renaming or closing, they ask herdr for the pane named by `HERDR_PANE_ID` and check that its shell is an ancestor of the caller; a dead pane or another session's pane (the id a shared `codex app-server` daemon passes to every child) is refused with a one-line message on stderr and nothing is changed.
- `fgos dispatch probe-account` no longer removes a private home kept for a pane that is still open once that home is past its maximum age: the sweep it runs after closing its own panes asks herdr about every other pane exactly as the regular sweep does, instead of treating them as unanswerable.
- A cli-spawn `fgos run` whose controlling process crashes or is killed mid-run no longer loses the worker: the detached run supervisor stops sending live output to the dead controller instead of crashing on the closed channel, so the worker keeps running, the deadline is still enforced, and the run's capture and receipt are still written.
- `fgos pick`/`take`, `fgos approve` (land) and `fgctl init` no longer wait up to 3 minutes after every commit on the main checkout, including the committing session's own. The fgOS pre-commit hook no longer writes `.fgos/main-checkout.lock`; it leaves a commit-activity beacon in `.fgos/runtime/main-checkout-activity.json` (writer, time and a `windowMs`, 20 s by default or `FGOS_MAIN_CHECKOUT_LOCK_TTL_MS`) that only the hook reads, to refuse another session's commit inside that window. `fgos lock-status` reports the beacon as `activity`, and `fgos return`/`cleanup`/`compound` clear the session's own beacon instead of the lock. The hook still refuses a commit, without waiting, while an fgOS claim, checkpoint or land holds the lock.
- Every holder of `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` or a merge slot now records its own `ttlMs` (the dispatch worktree lock is a kernel lock with no ttl, see above), and a contender judges the record by that ttl instead of its own (a dispatch with a longer timeout no longer outwaits a shorter holder, and a short contender no longer takes a longer holder's lock). A record left by an older release counts for 20 s when it is a session id (old hook) and 3 minutes when it is a pid.
- The `.fgos` events checkpoint that runs during `fgos approve` under a merge slot now holds `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` for its whole add, commit and reset, so it can no longer interleave with a land on the main checkout; when a land holds the lock the checkpoint is skipped until the next call. Claim and a merge without a slot reuse the lock they already hold.
- A lock record with a `v` field (even one that also has `pid` and `ts`), or a lock protocol marker (`.fgos/runtime/locks/<lock>/protocol.json`) naming any protocol other than 1, is refused with "upgrade fgOS" and is never reclaimed, released, renewed or overwritten by this release. The marker is checked before anything else, so the pre-commit hook, `fgos lock-status`, `fgos unlock`, the claim self-heal and `fgctl init` all refuse even when the lock file itself is absent or corrupt; `fgos unlock` never reports `cleared` there. Do not downgrade below this release once a newer lock protocol is in use.
- A native `fgos` verb that takes no stdin (for example `fgos convention path ...`) no longer waits for an inherited stdin to close: it hung under a heredoc, an agent Bash tool, or a pipe whose writer stays open. Only `metrics ping`, `metrics eval record`, and `friction record --detail-stdin` read stdin.
- A headless round that stops because the provider account used up its quota (codex "You've hit your usage limit") now settles as `provider-limit` with `failure.cause: quota` instead of a generic non-zero exit, so a Workflow unit or `fgos run` moves to another account or candidate, and a leased account waits out the reset time the provider printed.
- A dispatch round is no longer refused because files changed in a shared checkout while it ran (`wrote-outside-workspace`, `read-only-mutation`, `mutated-dirty-before-files`). A before/after snapshot cannot tell the worker's writes from another session's, so the round is accepted and the paths are reported in its result as `warnings` (`stray-write-correlated`, `read-only-mutation-correlated`, `mutated-dirty-before-correlated`) and on stderr. A write proven to be the run's own would still be refused; nothing proves one yet.
- An Assignment run's `result.json` now names the sandbox it really ran under in `confinement` (`bwrap`), read from the launch the Confinement Authority prepared or the dispatch's enforced attestation; it was always `null` before, even for sandboxed seats.
- A Work item stopped on a read-only round whose checkout changed while it ran now says so: the round is accepted with its `warnings`, and the driver stops with `assignment-<operation>-correlated-mutation` (at planning `validation-correlated-mutation-do-not-advance-work`) instead of a generic failed or no-evidence reason. A round launched through the executor CLI door now keeps that door's `stray-write-correlated` warning in its `result.json` instead of only printing it.
- `fgos run --resume` is refused while a live dispatch still holds the worktree's lock, so a second worker is never started in the same worktree; the old guard read a lock name no dispatch writes and never refused.
- A Unit's `persona` is resolved and its text pinned when the unit run starts, so a persona defined only in the workspace (`fgos/agents/`) is rendered with its definition instead of its bare name.
- A help token never runs the verb: `fgos init --json -h` created a store and `fgos session start --json -h` created a worktree, because the help token was read as the previous flag's value; through the Rust host, `fgos version --help` ran `version` and `fgos metrics runs --help` ran `runs`.
- Manifest entries now match what the CLI reads: `merge next` lists the flags it forwards to approve/sync-root, `workflow start --stance-options`, `workflow operations --step` (was `--stage`), `tool --config`, `tool check --name` (was a positional), `dispatch decide --assignment`, `run record --result`. AGENTS.md and the dispatch fallback skill say `decide --work <id> [--stage <stage>]` (was `--step`).
- `fgos main-checkout-reset` without `--confirm` moves forward again in a repository that tracks `.fgos` files: tracked `.fgos` paths that match HEAD are updated with the rest of the tree, and the reset refuses `restore-protected-fgos-path` only while a tracked `.fgos` path differs from HEAD.
- On a host without user namespaces (`linux-pgroup`), a ScopedCommit, Sync or Land whose hook or filter left a `setsid` or double-fork child alive after the borrow now returns `containment-unproven` as `recovery-required` instead of plain success; operations without hooks or filters are unchanged.

### Security

- The runner commit no longer trusts a worktree's `.git` file, a relative hooks path or fsmonitor: its git runs against the main repository's gitdir with the caller's `GIT_*` variables dropped, and a worktree outside the main repository is refused.
- The holder-lock routes (`lock-fd`, `lock-hold`, `state-root`, `process-observe`, `lock-borrow-vectors`) now speak internal protocol 2. A stale global npm `fgos` whose Node payload still sends `--protocol 1` is refused by the new host with `host-version-mismatch` before any lock is taken; reinstall or upgrade the npm package to match the active release. `quiesce-scan` stays on protocol 1.

A push the remote refuses for its own reason (a hook, a policy) reports that reason instead of a lost lease, a recovered repository-config change is acknowledged only after its file and directory are synced, and leftover temporary files of a failed journal write no longer count against the journal's size bound.
- Git operations name their failures the same way in every port: a busy journal, a reused operation id, a changed repository identity and an unavailable publication borrow answer `refused` with a named cause, and a corrupt or unwritable journal answers `recovery-required` with the journal's own text under `detail.diagnostic`; a borrowed Git run that times out says `git-timeout` and one that overruns its output says `git-output-limit`, as a contained run does; a publication read of a shallow repository names `shallow-history-incomplete`; a dangling symbolic ref reads as symbolic, not absent; a remote or mapping name longer than 80 bytes is refused.

- Admitting a lock over a dead predecessor whose process group or tree has a member that cannot die quickly now hands over or refuses within the 2000 ms kill wait. The kill used to wait up to 5 s for the domain to empty and only then start the 2000 ms, so a member stuck in uninterruptible I/O delayed the next holder by about 7 s.

- Removed the `fgos doctor` row `coordination-abandoned-claims`: nothing writes the coordination claim files it looked for any more, so it could only report on a mechanism that no longer exists. `fgos doctor --fix` no longer removes such entries.
- Removed the host route `fgos internal process-observe`: Node judges processes in-process through the native door, so nothing calls it. The doctor row `process-containment` and the lock route errors now end with the step to take.
- Durable writes now share one door: the case ledger's runtime files, gate answers, worktree bindings, run-control generations and release markers, immutable proofs, the provider capacity ledger, the credential copy and the gateway registry are written and fsynced (file and directory) by the durable-file crate, and a failed write names the step it failed at and whether the name was installed (`durable install failed at name-installed (installed: none)`) and leaves no retained temporary file. A create-only write that loses to an existing name no longer fsyncs a directory. Confinement attestation temporary names no longer collide across processes in the same millisecond.
- Process identity (`src/runner/dispatch/process-identity.mjs`) now judges, observes and signals through the Rust process-facts crate by way of one in-process native door (`src/native/door.mjs`, the same addon Git loads), not through Node's own `/proc` reads. On the npm/GitHub install channel, where the addon is not shipped, the door refuses by name with `process-door-not-shipped: onboard this project with fgctl init` and has no JavaScript fallback.
- `fgos gateway stop` and `fgos lock fence` signal only the process whose recorded identity (pid, start time, boot) still matches, and refuse by name otherwise: a gateway registry entry written without an identity (an older entry) is refused as `gateway-stop-identity-unknown` / `gateway-start-identity-unknown` with the file to delete, `gateway status` reports it as `identity: unknown`, and a registry entry is cleared only once the process is proven gone. A gateway or lock holder that has exited but is not yet reaped counts as stopped. The lock-fence confirmation prompt no longer shows the holder's command line.
- `fgos doctor` row `git-land-recovery` now also warns about finished Land operations whose candidate worktree and pins are still retained (operation id, candidate path, pins, age), and says there is no manual release command yet; the release sweep waits for the Work lane. Read-only, no cleanup.
- A scoped runner commit now fsyncs the staged blobs and trees (file, fan-out directory and `objects/`) before `git commit` moves the branch, and the commit object before the receipt: before, the staged files and the directory entries were never fsynced, so a power cut could leave the branch naming a commit with an empty or missing tree or blob, acknowledged or not. Recovery of an unacknowledged tip with an unreadable object now reports `commit-objects-unreadable` (recovery required, branch untouched) instead of a raw Git error. Publication and scoped commits share one loose-object durability step. The E1 power-cut script gains `--kind scoped` for the same check.
- A scoped runner commit no longer lets a power cut leave an empty blob or tree under its final object name: `git add` and `write-tree` now run with `core.fsync=loose-object` (each loose file is fsynced before Git links it). An object an earlier release already left empty is removed and restaged before the commit, or the commit is refused with `object-file-corrupt` before `git commit`; before, Git kept the empty file, so the next commit named an unreadable object.
- A project config that still carries `runner.rigorToTier` is refused by config validation, which names the key; delete it and declare `tier` per capability, role, persona or seat. `fgos setup` no longer converts a pre-seat config (it copies no `config.json.pre-seat-binding-*` backup and prints no conversion diff), and a project config with no `runner.patterns.seatBinding.schema` is no longer refused. A global `~/.fgos/config.json` that still carries `rigorToTier` keeps loading: the key is dropped in memory with one note on stderr and the file is not edited. `fgos setup` and the first-run writer put no `rigorToTier` into any file.
- Rigor no longer raises a seat's tier or its reasoning effort. A unit `rigor`, `fgos run --rigor`, a guide `rigorFloor`, a Work item's `rigor` or `risk: heavy`, and a capability `rigor` now only set how many checkers a reviewed unit gets and how strictly seats must differ; the tier comes from the config (`defaults.tier`, a capability's `tier`, or its `roles`, `personas` and `seats` entries) or from a workflow seat's recommended tier. Without an explicit `--effort` or a cell effort, a seat runs at its invocation's own default effort. A capability that relied on `rigor: high` for a flagship model now needs `tier: flagship`; the conversion lists every unit it affects.
- `runner.maxTier` caps a seat visibly: a tier above it is lowered to it, and the binding, the run evidence and `fgos dispatch explain` name the tier it was lowered from, the config line that set it and the `maxTier` line that applied (`max-tier-cap`). A capability's own `maxTier` may be above the global one. The tier order of precedence is now seat, persona, role, the workflow seat's recommendation, the capability, its `<prefix>:*` entry, then `defaults.tier`; the bare verb of a capability (`review` for `code:review`) is no longer a lookup key, and a capability with no `prefer` takes the families `tierFallback` lists for its tier.
- `--tier` and `--override '{"tier":...}'` above the tier a seat resolves to are refused with `tier-escalation-unauthorized`, as is a persona or capability a door chose (`fgos run --persona`, `fgos run --capability`, `workflow start --seats`) whose tier is above the one the seat resolves to without it, and an override that accepts a dependence between seats (`dependence-acceptance-unauthorized`). An override at or below the resolved tier still works, as do `--effort`, `--timeout` and `--account`. No override carries an `origin` of `human-cli` any more.
- `fgos doctor` no longer has the rows `runner-rigor-config` and `capability-rigor-ceiling` (rigor no longer maps to a tier or a ceiling); `model-policy-tier-coverage` and `workflow-pools-satisfy-independence` are replaced by `seat-binding-dry-bind`. The projected agent definitions (`scripts/project-agents.mjs`) no longer name a model: a persona's rigor does not choose one.

- `fgos setup` refreshes a project runner `$comment` that differs from the tier ladder, and leaves a config with no `$comment` alone. The global `~/.fgos/config.json` gets no seat-binding key.
- Panel and debate units must declare their `seats:`; `params.members`, `params.role`, `params.synthesizeRole` and the `panelist-N` keys of `roleTasks` are gone, and `roleTasks` and `workflow start --seats` are keyed by seat. A reviewed unit's checker seats are `reviewer`, `red-team` and `tester`; unit records and assignment directories are keyed by seat, and a record written before this change (no `seatSchema`) cannot be resumed (`record-predates-seat-binding`) but stays readable.
- A seat's account is named by the same decision as its executor and model: the lease takes exactly that account, a lease that cannot take it settles as `provider-capacity-lease-conflict` and the seat is bound again under the same policy, and a lease receipt the provider record does not back refuses a pass before anything is committed (`lease-receipt-mismatch`). New `unit.json` snapshots no longer store `llmAccounts` or `providers`. The second walker (`attemptProviderCapacityFallback`) and the operation policy key `fallbackExecutors` are removed.
- A Work operation or a raw dispatch that names no seat of its own now gets its executor, tier, model and effort from Seat Binding, through the same crate call a unit run makes. The executor it names, else the global `executor`, reaches Seat Binding as a pin; Seat Binding picks the tier, the model and the effort, and the Work path no longer takes the first model of a family's cell. A pinned executor Seat Binding cannot seat (`pin-unsatisfiable`), a capability with no executor to bind and a missing runner config (`runner-config-missing`) are refused by name. `executeExecutorCli` takes the tier and the model from the caller that bound the seat or from the executor entry, and refuses (`seat-not-bound`) when neither has them. The unit run's own seats are unchanged.
- `fgos doctor` rows: new `seat-binding-route`, `seat-binding-config` (the project runner `$comment` matches the tier ladder; a difference is noted, not failed) and `seat-binding-dry-bind`; removed `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot`. `tier-fallback` also warns when a declared `tierFallback` has no list for one of the six tiers. Workflow definitions packaged as a directory (`<name>/wf.<name>.yaml`) are now read by the doctor checks that read Workflow files.

- A persona file that names a model `tier` or `prefer` is now refused with `persona-model-taste-not-allowed` (model taste belongs to the seat, at `capabilities.<cap>.personas.<name>`), a packaged workflow (`<name>/wf.<name>.yaml`) can keep its own personas beside it (`agent.<name>.yaml`), and a domain persona is visible only to workflows of that domain.

- `fgos worktree remove --delivered-to` takes the same names as `worktree create --base` (a short remote-tracking name such as `origin/main` was refused before); both resolve through one literal-ref resolver. Recovery of a publication whose pin release is stuck now reports that chain by id and still settles the others.
- A brief is never typed into a herdr pane's shell any more: terminal-control refuses a `send` (prompt door included) unless a program other than the pane's shell holds the foreground, and the run ends as a failed attempt with reason `terminal:foreground-not-agent`; the gate also drops tty input its agent never read before the pane's shell gets the tty back, so a brief typed at an agent that never started can no longer run as shell commands (backtick spans included).
- Event Store seals and every Git publication now survive a power cut: trees are written through the same fsynced object write as blobs and commits (git `mktree` never fsynced them), and a pin release interrupted by a crash resumes on the next release instead of staying `recovery-required`. Proven on ext4 by the Git E1 power-cut replay (1029 points, 0 violations) and the Event Store power-loss run (20/20).
- Git (branch `git/p07-switch` fixes from the host gate):
  - A commit hook may print up to 64 MiB again (Git sends hook output to stderr); a borrowed Git run no longer fails at 64 KiB.
  - A hook or filter child that drops the lock descriptor and leaves its process group now turns a commit, Sync or Land into `containment-unproven` (`recovery-required`) on every machine, also where bwrap can make a PID namespace; before, only machines without it were watched.
  - The runner commits and syncs when the session has no env id (the writer is then a process id): every Git port now gets the writer as text.
  - A Workflow whose units declare no `writes` (for example `business-discussion`) now runs in a directory that is not a git repository, which becomes its project root; a unit with `writes` or a sync ref is still refused there before any unit run exists.
  - On the npm/GitHub install channel, `fgos init` in a project that `fgctl init` has not activated now refuses with `git-addon-unavailable: addon not shipped on this channel: onboard this project with fgctl init` (it said "until M10") and changes nothing; onboard new projects with `fgctl init`.
  - `scripts/build-rust-distribution.mjs` loads the addon it just built from the staged `libexec/native/fgos.node` (Node read the `.so` name as JavaScript) and reads the checkout with it in a child process, since a process holds one addon.

- `fgos doctor` check `git-mutation-one-door` reads the release's `packages/git/contracts/mutation-census.v1.json`, which the release build writes from `scripts/git-one-door-scan.mjs`. The check fails when the census lists any `git` or hook spawn outside the fgos-git driver, or was not built from the payload it ships in. `npm test` also fails when product code (`src`, `bin`, `scripts`) starts `git` or a hook while the suite runs, and names the call site.
  - Commands from operator configuration or from a Work item's declared verify command count as configured binaries, not sites.
  - Executor commands are traced to the runner config files and their defaults. The holder-lock borrow vectors, which run `git` only in a temp repository they create, count as the production sandbox probe; that class now needs the repository's own data flow to a `temp_dir()` path, never `temp_dir()` and `init` merely appearing in the same function.
  - The scan lists every file of the checkout through Inspect and skips no directory by its name. It judges what the checkout declares as product (the payload `package.json` ships, every crate the Cargo workspace names, the installed hooks); the census counts the other files (tests, fixtures, records, `tools/`) per top-level directory. Built from this tree it lists two sites: the same `git mv` sentence in `domains/coding/skills/fgos-coding-planning/references/bootstrap-and-lane.md` and its `.agents/skills` render, until that sentence is reworded.
  - The scan also follows `promisify(execFile)` across modules, a `shell: true` held in an options variable, and a computed member on `child_process` (an unreadable one is a site). A hook's `reflog` and `symbolic-ref` count as reads only in their read forms.
  - Scripts of a skill that declares `metadata.oneDoor: standalone` in its SKILL.md (`distill`, `instruction-audit`) are counted as `standalone-skill-script`, not as sites; the test spy now watches `core/skills/` too.
  - The scan now follows functions passed around as values and methods of returned objects. The phase 07 unit 22 report names each open site.

- `fgos main-checkout-reset` resets through the Git SafeRestore port instead of a raw `git reset --hard`.
  - With `--confirm` it keeps the old HEAD pinned and snapshots the discarded local changes, and its result carries an `operationId` and a `snapshot`.
  - `--confirm` is an operator flag, not proof that a human confirmed: any caller that can run the verb, an agent included, can pass it. A confirmed reset may move to any commit, sideways or backward. The old HEAD stays pinned at `refs/fgos/git-operations/<operationId>/candidate` with its snapshot until the SafeRestore `acknowledge` operation releases them; no verb calls it yet, so the pin and snapshot stay.
  - It also clears a stopped merge, cherry-pick or revert.
  - The list of commits it would drop no longer shows `--stat` and stops at 50 lines.
  - An unknown `--sha` is refused before anything runs.

- The gateway and the herdr dashboard find the main checkout through fgos-git instead of running `git rev-parse`.

- `fgos return` verifies a branch in a checkout made and removed through the Worktree port. A checkout that still holds bytes after verify is kept and named instead of force-removed. The verify checkout is now provisioned like a Land candidate (dependency install, then the project's `worktreeSetup.commands`), and what that placed is recorded and set aside on removal, so the checkout no longer stays behind with its `node_modules`. Dispatch worktrees and the already-merged verification checkout of `approve` are torn down the same way. `fgos preflight`, `resync-worktree`, `compound --doc-path` and `knowledge attest` read Git through Inspect. `resync-worktree` run where no branch is checked out now asks for `--branch`.

- `scripts/install-git-hooks.mjs` reports a RepositoryConfig refusal (for example `git-fence-missing` in a checkout that was never activated) as one line with exit 1, not a stack trace. The shell integration's `fgos` and `fgos-runner` functions find the main checkout from the `.git` layout on disk instead of running `git`.

- The activation gate (`fgctl`) and `fgos events migrate` stop check also scan processes working in the workspace's linked worktrees.

- Workflow integration merges through Land and skips work the target already has.

- `fgos approve` retried after a refusal that came before Land started (a held merge slot under `--no-wait`, a busy main checkout, a stopped merge, a conflict found before the candidate) reuses the Land operation it recorded and delivers, instead of failing on a journal that was never written. The decision log gains one engine decision for each Land operation approve starts, and one for each blocked `sync-root` result.
  - An approve whose earlier Land was interrupted mid-publication refuses and names `fgos doctor --fix`. Its new `git-land-recovery` fix recovers interrupted Land operations under Land's own locks: one that never attempted its publication closes as abandoned; an attempted one only by the writer that started it, and the fix names that writer otherwise. `fgos setup` runs the same fix.
  - A failure while publishing that Land cannot classify is reported as an unknown effect (`land-effect-unknown`, naming `fgos doctor --fix`), no longer as a failed merge that parks the item `blocked`. A failure of the drift report after a land is reported beside the land in `postLand.error`.

- A SafeRestore (`resync-worktree`, `main-checkout-reset` and every other restore) refuses with `restore-orphaned-patch` while an interrupted restore's patch for that branch is left under the Git directory's `fgos-resync-patches/`. The refusal names the patches; apply what is still wanted from each, then delete them and restore again.

- `fgos uninstall` leaves a `core.hooksPath` that fgOS did not record setting.

- The quiesce scan takes `--dir` for each linked worktree.

- Commands that make many Git reads reuse the repository's checked config and storage format across them within one process, re-reading only when a config file changes: `approve --no-wait` refusing a held merge slot went from about 0.7 s to 0.4 s (79 to 21 Git processes) and `doctor --json` from about 3.8 s to 2.4 s (332 to 62).
- New skill `fgos-cook`: delivers a plan written by `ak:plan` by opening a conductor case on the coding guide with an owner-approved frame, then dispatching one slice at a time through `fgos run` and `fgos workflow` naming the case, checking each result itself and handing the branch to the owner (it never merges). Slices run serially in one worktree until the Git land operation exists; the route table waits for Seat Binding.
- A conductor Workflow case now moves past its entry milestones: when a Unit settles with `pass` (or `findings`), its activity's `produces` milestones are proposed as achieved with the digest of their subject (the Unit's reports, or for a delivery milestone the paths it wrote, backed by a verify receipt for that digest). Before, the settle recorded nothing, so `fgos run --case C --activity implement-item` stayed refused with `entry-milestone-unmet` after `validate-plan` passed.
- A panel or debate unit must now declare its `seats:` (ids, roles, optional persona), and `workflow start --seats` re-seats generic member seats; a reviewed unit may declare its seats too, if its checker roles match what its rigor requires. Resuming a unit run recorded before seat binding is refused with `record-predates-seat-binding` (it stays readable in summaries, history and metrics).

- `fgos doctor` has a new row `seat-binding-route`: it asks the host that Seat Binding will run (the activation host inside an activated release, `FGOS_HOST_BIN` outside one) to answer the internal `seat-binding ladder` route at protocol 1, and fails with `host-version-mismatch` on a host built before the route. A worker no longer inherits `FGOS_HOST_BIN`.

- `npm run fgos:dev` now makes Node clients (identity, repository access, run supervisor, terminal control) use the working-tree host it staged, not the activated release's host. Resuming a unit run whose `unit.json` carries a `seatSchema` from a newer release is refused with `record-from-newer-release`; reading such a record still works.

- A pi or omp seat in a herdr pane now gets its brief through the agent prompt door (one send that types and submits), as codex does. The raw typed brief took 7 to 25 s and sometimes lost its final Enter, and a seat stopped mid-typing could leave the rest of the brief in the pane's shell. The supervisor also re-reads its stop state before every send into the pane.

- `npm test` now prepares the release fgos, fgctl and native addon it tests against (incremental), so the suite is green on a fresh machine, not only in CI.

- `npm test` ends with a `suite:` line: test files, `test()` calls and wall time against the committed `test/suite-baseline.json`. It fails when a test body is copied byte for byte into a second file and the baseline does not list that clone, and warns on titles shared across files and on new unmarked `fgos init` or network calls in tests. `node scripts/test-proof-inventory.mjs --duplicates` lists the clones and shared titles; `--write-baseline [--wall-seconds <s>]` refreshes the baseline.

- `fgos worktree remove` no longer refuses every worktree `fgos worktree create` made. Create records what provisioning placed (each copied file with its content digest, and the installed `node_modules` declared regenerable) under the state root. Remove sets exactly those bytes aside before the Git port's clean check, puts them back if the port refuses, and deletes them once the checkout is gone. A copied file a worker edited, or any other ignored byte, still makes the port refuse with `worktree-ignored-bytes-preserved`. A worktree made before this change has no record and still needs its provisioned bytes cleaned by hand once.

- `fgos doctor` check `lock-fences` no longer counts a run made by the run supervisor (it holds `attempt.lock`) as a missing `.recovery.lock` tombstone. Per-run tombstones belong only to runs that existed at the cutover, so the warning no longer grows with every new run. `run-attempts-stuck` now also names a removed payload checkout of an attempt's release, not only a removed host binary.

- Close settled run panes when the gate proves the worker ended and stdout/stderr are captured, including cancellation and non-zero exits; retain crash diagnostics and uncertain attempts. A settlement step that has not completed yet no longer fixes the pane as retained: the pass that completes it decides. `npm run fgos:dev` keeps its staged host while a detached run supervisor still runs from it.

- Reduce dormant Event Store read overhead through validated retained views and current-command Git fact reuse; verify only new active-log tails, preserve append durability, and fix concurrent store benchmark cursors with explicit outside-read timings.

- Keep Event Store retired-path enforcement dormant until the tracked cutover fence; preserve append root durability, tolerate partial maintenance headers, and expose an absent local origin as `null`. Dormant door checks tolerate unrelated Work edits.

- Harden the dormant Event Store: reuse verified reads and stamped Git configuration, avoid syncing untouched directories, expose local maintenance facts and canonical branch keys, and block retired event paths and event-ref bypasses. Store latency benchmarks can seed realistic history without a Work consumer.

- `fgos worktree create` now provisions the new checkout after the Git port returns: dependency install, then the project's `worktreeSetup.commands`. This repo's setup also copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout, so a worker in that worktree can use `ak:cook`. The setup no longer builds the Rust workspace in each new worktree (a run that needs a binary builds it with its own Cargo target). `fgos setup` no longer deletes skills other tools installed into `.agents/skills` (only entries fgOS itself assembled are pruned). The claude executor declares `ak:cook` in `supports.skills`, and `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill is missing from the runtime's skill directory. `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md` is the brief for an `ak:cook` worker.
- Add the `debate` collaboration pattern: a thesis side and an antithesis side argue blind in parallel, answer each other's round-1 argument (`params.rebuttal: false` skips it), and a read-only judge on a provider family different from both sides rules; a pool that cannot seat such a judge is refused by name. `group-cognition`'s dialectical step now runs `debate` instead of `reviewed`, and its action synthesis builds on the judge's ruling.

- `fgos version` (and the `cli-version-visible` doctor row) shows the first 12 hex digits of the checkout's full commit id instead of Git's variable-length short id. `fgos init` and every other Git read now work on a machine where the fgOS state root does not exist yet: it is created owner-only, as `fgos doctor --fix` would.

- `approve`, `sync-root` and `merge next` with `--no-wait` refuse a held merge slot of the target before reading anything else, so the refusal comes at once.

- `scripts/knowledge-migration.mjs` commits each document move as its own commit instead of leaving staged renames. The nightly mutation run no longer force-removes its checkouts: one that still holds run bytes is kept and reported. The `distill` skill pulls only the reference clones under its own `upstreams/` directory.

- `catchup` (and the inline catchup in leaf `approve` and `sync-root`) keeps the target's `.fgos` bytes the way Land does: a branch that deleted an event shard the target grew no longer fails as `merge-refused`, a leaf whose root branch was never created approves instead of parking `fgos-write-rejected`, a conflict is reported without leaving a catch-up checkout behind, and a refused merge reports Git's own message. `cleanup` deletes the merged branch only at the tip it verified.

- Leaf `approve`, `sync-root` and `promote-to-component` now land through Git Land like root-into-main `approve`: the target branch's merge slot is Land's (`lock fence merge-slot --param ref=` now takes the URL-encoded full ref, e.g. `refs%2Fheads%2Fmain`), the item's verify runs in Land's candidate, a root branch checked out in another worktree is refused instead of moved behind it, and `.fgos` event files due for a checkpoint are committed before the merge rather than inside it. After `approve` or `sync-root` records the result, Land's published candidate is removed.

- Root-into-main `approve` through Land again refuses a branch that writes under `.fgos/`, self-resolves decision-id collisions on the decision index and `merge=union` `.fgos` conflicts, and runs the repo-invariant checks on the candidate before publishing.

- `approve`/`merge` `--wait` now also bounds Land's wait for the main checkout at publication (previously a fixed 5 s), and a waiting Land no longer stalls its own process, so a release by another holder in the same process is seen.

- Git Land can pin the current destination under its own slot, wait for admission without retrying publication, and freeze exact consumer-declared conflict resolutions before verification. Merge review patches, changed-path lists, ancestry and clean-tree reads now use Git Inspect; the legacy publication callers have not yet been switched.

- Forced session cleanup retains detached commits with a named recovery ref and snapshot, and preserves dirty sessions. Missing checkout registrations are pruned only with inspected ownership evidence. Work event checkpoints and verified archive publication use declared native Git transactions.

- Mutating Units refuse the main checkout before native Git preflight; resuming under a live worktree holder reports `dispatch-in-flight`.

- Scoped Unit commits exclude tracked and untracked `.fgos` paths under broad scopes; legacy event commits require main-checkout authority. ScopedCommit and Sync classify owned hook refusals consistently, and unknown recovery ids fail explicitly.

- Unit commits and syncs use the native Git component with persisted baselines, custody-backed recovery and literal filenames. Original hook failure output is preserved; foreign hooks are never replayed. Legacy Work event checkpoints use an explicit, main-only temporary declaration.

- Add `fgos worktree remove <path> --delivered-to <ref>`: removes a worktree through the Worktree port, which refuses a dirty checkout, one a process stands in, preserved worker state, or a tip not contained in the delivery target (branch name, full ref or object id). No force flag; the delivery statement is recorded as the operation's evidence digest.

- Git typed commit and recovery reads ignore user signature/display settings; suite subprocess census no longer requires strace.

- Git typed operations batch storage and commit-header reads, reuse operation-local checkout facts and index evidence, and expose paired per-phase Git/holder-lock census diagnostics.

- Git hooks ownership excludes included config files; interrupted native-lock exchanges resume automatically using the recorded guard identity. GitHub merge diagnostics retain pre-connect failures and stop polling terminal PRs, and restore extraction preserves missing worktree registrations as exclusions.

- Git recovery preserves live Publication and non-event transfer lock contracts, releases terminal ref pins, tolerates prunable extraction registrations, and atomically guards Linux native-lock quarantine; GitHub merge timeouts query server state before a later request.

- Git deadline cleanup now gives children three seconds to terminate cooperatively; unowned native index locks refuse with `native-index-lock-unowned` and a read-only holder report plus the retained-lock runbook.

- Git Recovery reconciles ConfigChange under repo-config authority; hooks configuration preserves inherited values and removes only owned local settings. Native quarantine detects inode substitution after rename.

- SafeRestore extraction refuses sibling worktrees and the state root, binds creation to a directory descriptor, and recognizes tracked case-only aliases. Add a dormant partial Recovery facade, a GitHub timeout/query contract test, and paired typed-operation E3 budget rows.

- Git adds dormant native index-lock inspection/quarantine and owned hooks configuration APIs, with exact inode/value guards and WAL recovery; existing setup and mutation callers remain on their current paths.

- Git Land can recover an observed candidate after later destination commits without touching checkout/index; unrelated main merge/bisect state no longer blocks prepare/publish or terminal receipt replay.

- SafeRestore refuses untracked/ignored collisions unless exact replacement paths are authorized, captures only local bytes, preserves incoming executable modes and intent-to-add, and exposes snapshot extraction and acknowledgement-gated cleanup. Unreadable snapshots no longer permanently block a checkout.

- Git Land recovery blocks unreconciled predecessor effects, tolerates index stat refresh, preserves ignored store collisions and permits acknowledged cleanup of abandoned/lost candidates.

- Add dormant SafeRestore preview/apply/recover ports with durable binary/index/untracked/mode snapshots, verified checkout custody, local delta reapplication and observe-only crash recovery.

- Git Land preserves unrelated staged changes, closes abandoned prepares at admission, and reports attempted retries and CAS failures consistently with recovery.

- Add dormant Land recovery through the existing Rust/addon/Node port, observe-only CAS recovery, recorded checkout fingerprints, acknowledgement-gated cleanup and compacted receipt replay.

- Add dormant Git Land prepare/publish ports with immutable candidates, consumer verification binding, own-file checkout protection, one-shot CAS and operation-id receipt replay; production callers remain unchanged.

- The coordination driver doctrine (`core/skills/_shared/coordination-driver.md`, loaded by `fgos-advise` and the other coordination facades) now teaches the case model: observe with `fgos workflow status <caseId>`, choose an activity and route yourself, dispatch with `--case` and `--activity` on every run (read-only included), treat a refusal as an answer, ask a person only for the listed triggers, close with `fgos workflow close`. It no longer tells a driver to run `fgos workflow operations` on a run.

- Provider accounts of one pool are now taken in the order the config declares them, no longer by fewest leases or oldest use: the first account takes every lease until it is quarantined or disabled, then the next. A pool declared in `runner.llmAccounts` now supplies its own accounts to the lease (a `codex` store as a Codex home, any other store with the login files its invocations declare); a pool it does not declare keeps reading `runner.providers`. An account id of digits only is refused, since such a key would sort ahead of the others. `runner.tierFallback` (tier to ordered list of families) is checked by the new doctor row `tier-fallback`.

- A seat that fails on a provider limit or a dead login now walks the tier it runs at: first the remaining models of its family's cell for that tier (each `model@pool` entry is served by its own pool and its own accounts), then the families `runner.tierFallback.<tier>` lists, limited to the families the capability's `prefer` names and never leaving the tier. A pool no enabled account of can run (no account holding the CLI's login store) is not a candidate, and a dead login excludes that pool only, not the family's other pools. The leading family of a seat still follows `prefer`. `fgos run --account` and `fgos workflow start --account` now take `pool/account` (for example `openai/work`); a bare account id is refused with the form to write. A tier with no model for an out-of-process agent seat's family now refuses with `tier-cell-missing`, naming `runner.modelPolicies.<family>.<tier>`; `executor.model` and the `default` model no longer stand in for a missing cell. `fgos dispatch explain` prints the candidates in order (with why one is out), the walk, and the accounts of each pool on it in lease order. A unit record written before this change restarts its walk at the primary.

- `fgos doctor` row `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` now recomputes a fallback attempt with the seat's earlier bindings, the way the write gate does, so it no longer reports a binding mismatch for every attempt after the first; a binding that differs from its walk still fails. The messages of `model-policy-pools` and `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` now say that the walk skips a pool with no usable account and that the lease reads `runner.llmAccounts` for a pool it declares.
- Git checkout operations revalidate config file stamps before each child and refuse post-hook promisor changes while retaining the reduced preflight exec count.

- Git: reuse config and storage-format checks within each ScopedCommit/Sync call, recheck after hooks, and retain per-child topology and custody validation.
- A Unit that writes is no longer run without asking whether a Workflow case owns its worktree. `runUnit` takes the admission port from its caller (the Execution Core owns the interface, the Workflow implements it, every entry point injects it): a writing Unit without the port is refused as `case-admission-port-missing`, a standalone writing run goes on only into a worktree no case binds, and a Unit that names a case is admitted before custody and the unit directory, linked in `unit.json` as `{ caseId, activity, reservationId }` (older records still read), held to a seat-launch ceiling (planned seats times the frame's fallback allowance; a provider limit keeps `fallbackExhausted`, a reviewed run that cannot start its next round ends at its last evaluation), rechecked at the write gate (`consent-stale` commits nothing) and settled once. The Playbook proposer, `fgos run`, the Work dispatch, operation-choice and fan-out paths all inject the real port; the Work paths get `unbound` and behave as before.

- `fgos run --case <id> --activity <id> [--route should|may-instead|unlisted] [--reason <text>]` and `fgos workflow start --case <parentId>` name the case a run belongs to. Every signal a call gives (the reference, the case variables its door set, the binding of the worktree it writes) must name one open case: `authority-context-conflict` and `authority-context-invalid` (unknown, malformed, closed: never standalone), `bound-worktree-requires-case-authority` for a writing run into a bound worktree that names no case, `playbook-case-admits-via-proposer-only` for a call from outside a Playbook case's proposer, and `nested-write-from-confined-worker` for a writing dispatch from inside a confined worker. Workers no longer inherit `FGOS_CASE_ID`/`FGOS_CASE_RESERVATION`: the door sets them from the reservation it admitted (codex gets them beside its writer id in injected config). A nested case or `--units` wave is charged to its parent's frame first and given back, exactly once, when it cannot open.

- A Playbook case that ran to a pass now closes itself, by the same rules as `fgos workflow close` (quiet bindings released); a failed, blocked or parked case stays open for `resume` and `answer`, and a conductor case still closes only through `fgos workflow close`.

- A gate approval can be given again for content that changed after it was approved. The digest of an edited report is now the digest of the bytes that lie there (it used to become unknown), so the gate asks again, the re-approval is bound to the new digest, and the next Unit is handed the revision a person approved instead of being refused as `report-changed-after-settle`; an edit no approval covers is still refused.

- `fgos doctor` row `git-worktree-recovery` no longer fails on a worktree whose `git worktree lock` reason names a process that is still running (pid and start time checked, a reused pid does not count); a lock naming a dead or unparseable owner stays a finding.

- Event Store migration refuses published mirror conflicts before changing the local legacy ref, restores pre-commit filesystem failures, and computes dry-run identities through Rust and the read-only Git port.

- Fix dormant Event Store migration retries and recovery ownership, pre-cutover doctor warnings, HEAD-only reads, and restorable nested porting rollback exports.

- Add dormant Event Store migration/import and rollback parity support, HEAD-only legacy reads, migration-required write refusals, and legacy-layout diagnostics; CLI registration follows at cutover.

- `fgos workflow` plays by the case model. The playbook runner is now the Playbook proposer: it asks admission for every Unit (entry milestones, consent bound to the approved artifact, independent seats, disjoint writes, worktree binding, the approved frame), records a route and a reservation before the Unit runs and a settle with its receipts after, and parks the gate again when an approval no longer matches the artifact it approved; the order the playbooks run in does not change. `workflow answer` keeps the answer as a file and, while a proposer is alive, leaves it to record the answer before it acts (nothing else is started); `status` adds a `case` block (milestones with digests, listed routes and the unlisted path, frame left, open gates, live reservations); new `fgos workflow close <id>` (refused while a closure milestone is stale or a consent gate is parked); `start` takes `--frame key=value,...` to narrow the guide's frame, never widen it. A guide with its own activities opens a conductor case: a case id and no driving process. `src/workflow/runner.mjs` is split by role into `unit-handoff`, `case-lock`, `case-start`, `case-verbs`, with the proposer loop left in `runner.mjs`.
- A Workflow case now has a model behind its ledger: milestones bound to the digest of their subject, reservations, the approved frame with its counters, routes and deviations, receipts from named evaluators only, and an admission check that answers whether a proposed activity may run now (entry milestones, consent bound to the approved artifact, independent seats, disjoint write scopes, binding, frame). A worktree is bound to one case through one record file per worktree identity. A gate answer is now one file per round that is never rewritten, and a second answer to an answered gate is refused (`gate-already-answered`). `fgos doctor` gains `workflow-case-binding-sentinel` and `workflow-case-bindings` (and `--fix` for the latter).
- Git: defer foreign-checkout cleanup failures after durable closure, preserve Sync receipt replay across branch changes, name detached-HEAD refusal, and document reflog-only recovery.

- Restore WAL exclusion between checkout and worktree lifecycle operations; refuse reflog-only commit attribution, bind Sync recovery to its recorded branch, close foreign attempted chains honestly, and retain sync warnings in runner results.

- Bind checkout WAL to directory identity, recover hook-modified and reflog-visible commits, preserve terminal causes and landed receipts across compaction failures, protect async siblings during native Git loans, and retain clean-file permissions during rollback. Add an aged-floor Node-loan E3 row for host acceptance.

- Git: recover interrupted scoped commits without replay, unblock pre-attempt/rejected Sync transactions, bound terminal WAL history, preserve concurrent sibling borrows, and restore clean merge paths on abort. E3 now measures Node-loaned checkout custody.

- Restore declared producer bytes, modes and move paths after rejecting ScopedCommit hooks; drain adopted setsid lock borrowers without harming unrelated pre-exec children.

- Preserve acquisition reach provenance in native holder-lock handover and emit Git WAL addon capabilities from the shared release/dev/test producer. Prevent uncertain Sync commit retries after a controller crash and preserve actual hook-modified file sets on receipt replay. Phase 05 remains unreleased pending its remaining acceptance proofs.

- Add dormant native ScopedCommit, Sync and non-event Checkpoint ports, a Rust write-scope leaf, and an activated-host cutover grant check. Linux-x64 activation refuses a missing addon or missing `git-wal-v1` addon capability. Production adapter migration remains phase 07.

- Workflow definitions load into one guide model (milestones, activities, decision points, MUST rows that each name an existing check, unenforced rules, frame defaults). Playbooks keep their steps and gain a short guide head; a MUST naming a check outside the catalog, an expression field, `listedRoutesOnly` outside a decision point, or `rigorCeiling` is a load error. A run's start event records the normalised guide.

- `fgos workflow start --plan` is removed (an unknown flag now): the AgentKit plan is read as an artifact and its phases run as Units through `fgos run` or `fgos workflow start --units <file>`. The coding workflow file drops its dead runner fields (`units`, `dependsOn`, `gate` and the `integrate` and `approval` steps); its lifecycle part is unchanged.
- End terminal rounds with `terminal:result-unreadable` when an invalid result stays unchanged for 30 seconds and the agent is idle, releasing custody through normal settlement.
- Preserve committed decision-index rows missing from local state during setup and doctor fixes; exclude git-ignored setup output consistently from release payloads and checkout drift checks.
- Warn once per unreadable pid per Worktree removal or relocation, and allow clean tracked `.fgos` while preserving reappearing skip-worktree state and dirty bytes.
- Arm the Linux terminal gate’s parent-death signal so a killed sandbox monitor ends its namespace; read all kernel lock-table pages while retaining shared-probe release confirmation.

- Warn with pid and comm when a same-user process cwd is unreadable during Worktree removal or relocation; readable checkout cwds still refuse.

- Fix Worktree allocation under `.claude/worktrees`, multi-user cwd checks and terminal recovery of clean Git refusals; require reachable delivery before removal and report preserved dirty checkouts as advisory diagnostics.

- Add `fgos worktree create <path> [--branch <name> | --detach] [--base <ref>]`: serialized worker checkout creation with stripped `.fgos`, plus read-only `git-worktree-recovery` diagnostics. Dormant native Worktree removal, relocation and evidence-bound crash recovery preserve dirty or uncertain checkouts.
- Ctrl-C and SIGTERM of `fgos run` now stop the run cleanly: no commit, reviewer, verify or next round starts after the signal, a signal during the hand-over of an attempt cancels it once it binds, and the resume line is always printed. A malformed `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` or `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` is a named validation error, and `fgos doctor` names an attempt whose release was removed and how to recover it. Library callers of the runner keep their own signal handling.

- Fix custody admission for busy worktrees, preserve settled results on handoff errors, distinguish reused cwd inodes, and restore 64 MiB commit output capture with overflow errors on every platform.

- Writing Unit runs retain cwd custody through runner commits and lend it to git/hooks and to the Unit verify command; successor admission preserves unprovable predecessor worktrees. Mutating producers require a supervised domain, and `--force-shared-cwd` with writes is refused. Workflow redispatches an unknown custody predecessor in a fresh worktree while preserving its old checkout and branch. Custody refusals include cwd, executor and capability context.

- Preserve historical Publication transfer WAL digests; classify transport config by Git scope across linked worktrees and symlinked paths. Doctor now explains refused repo-local CI credentials: use actions/checkout `persist-credentials: false` with a trusted global credential helper or `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`-level setting.

- Harden Git Remote against repository URL/transport redirects; make pushes atomic, settle forced remote-tracking fetches with exact-old checks, and tighten checkout and branch-use preflight with one shared transfer WAL shape.

- Git adds dormant typed Refs and non-event Remote facades: checked-out branches are protected under worktree-admin, fast-forward checkout updates require custody, transfers use explicit mappings and preserve unknown outcomes without resending. Opaque one-shot native lock handover blocks release during calls and rejects forged handles; Windows handover remains unsupported.

- Git adds a dormant typed Inspect facade with byte-safe status/diff/object/path/worktree reads, explicit trunk uncertainty and shallow ancestry errors, bounded streamed write snapshots on Unix, and transaction-local Rust lock scopes seeded only by verified holder handles. Diff hardening flags now precede the path delimiter. Linked-worktree cwd discovery validates reciprocal main registration; separate-git-dir remains unsupported.
- Bind Event Store appends to prepared machine authority, remove raw store construction, require trusted-main preparation, and tighten gate/error/consumer validation.

- Harden Git landing repairs: ignore reserved legacy mirror suffixes, diagnose their refs, migrate historical origin mappings alongside custom remotes, preserve symlinked state roots, and refuse unrelated-root chmod with actionable hooks diagnostics.

- Fix Git setup so ordinary fetch/pull work before the legacy Event Store ref exists; repair previously installed exact refspecs, share Git’s mapping policy across setup and Event Store, and repair/diagnose unsafe Git driver directory modes on umask-002 hosts.

- Git rollback WAL scans ignore durable-file temporaries in the compaction ledger using the same rule as other WAL readers; incomplete or corrupt installed entries still refuse.
- Git Publication now checks changing candidates through the successful connectivity fast path, makes replayed Intent directories durable, preserves full recoverable receipts through compaction, and tolerates scans racing terminal compaction. Recreated loose objects get fresh directory durability; deferred compaction failures are reported.
- The optional `git-floor-verdict.json` cache binds Git/config/PATH and host/probe identities and requires the exact probe set; include directives disable persistent reuse. Holder-lock uses one lagged scan for borrow cleanup and quiescent admission, then settles exclusive Linux release (including dropped guards) using positive kernel-table evidence plus an inode-checked shared probe (brief Try contention), killing escaped descriptor recipients at release; Publication close returns the cleanup outcome. Holder-lock also fixes its Windows time imports. Mapped process spawning resolves relative PATH entries in the child directory and runs executable scripts without a shebang.
- A confined invocation can declare the login store it reads with `credentialStore` (`use`, `homeEnv`, optional `files`) in the runner config; the sandbox points that variable at its private home and copies the store's files, and an invocation that declares none gets no login. Files of the store that are absent are now skipped instead of refusing the launch; a store with none present still refuses, with a named reason. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the store of the bound invocation, and `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` covers every confined invocation that reads a store. Older configs that bind `private-home` to an env variable keep working. This repo's own config now declares stores, drops the account name from invocation ids (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`, `pi-cli-bwrap`) and no longer carries the OpenRouter key variable for pi.
- Codex terminal runs deliver the brief through the terminal-control prompt door instead of typing it and pressing Enter, so a long brief is no longer left unsubmitted in the composer; the paste-chip matcher also recognizes codex's `[Pasted Content N chars]`.
- Releases ship a combined Git/Event Store Node addon through optional `components.nativeAddon`; its manifest attests build inputs without binding future upgrades to the verifier's Cargo.lock. Only Linux advertises `git-wal-v1` while C5 scan/fence support is Linux-only; Windows activation remains available and lock-taking Git ports refuse with `git-lockscope-unavailable-windows`.
- Config mapping failures resolve their WAL chain and remove only their own native staging lock. Re-running activation installs a missing Git fence; WAL writers refuse an unfenced workspace. Older `fgctl` stops with `EISDIR` at the fenced legacy activation lock. Channels without the optional addon report informational Git checks until M10.

- Git doctor now checks the combined addon ABI and Git floor, repository topology, WAL backlog/retained bytes, native lock residue, publication fetch mappings and durability limits (`git-component-compatible`, `git-trust-topology`, `git-operation-journal`, `git-native-locks`, `git-publication-refspecs`, `git-durability-capability`). Registered setup fixes initialize the WAL and, on `fgos setup`, install the additive origin mirror mappings `+refs/fgos/events/*:refs/fgos/remotes/origin/events/*` and `+refs/fgos/legacy:refs/fgos/remotes/origin/legacy` through the Rust config writer.

- Git WAL admission in `fgctl` uses `activation-v2.lock` and fences old controllers at first WAL-capable activation. Pending operations block rollback to a release without `git-wal-v1`; corrupt or incomplete WAL scans refuse activation. Atomic fence placement currently requires Linux.
- The Rust Git component can install additive Event Store fetch mappings under `repo-config` 80, preserving user settings and recording the effective remote URL in WAL provenance. The combined Node binding and doctor/setup integration are registered.
- Event Store sync authenticates its own reconciliation merges (the exact verified prior tip and candidate are authorized before the ref CAS), verifies each mirror independently so a rewound or forged foreign mirror becomes a typed warning instead of blocking own publication, and reports every tracked-fence mismatch as `event-store-legacy-mismatch`. Re-running fetch-mapping setup when mappings already exist records an effect-free `configApproved` WAL outcome.

### Added
- `fgos run "<prompt>" --input <a>,<b> --verify "<cmd>"` hands the Unit its input files and the command that checks its work; both are Unit fields (`inputs`, `verify`) that units files and workflow templates carry too, and a Unit may also name `skills`, which only executors declaring them in `supports.skills` can serve (refusal reason `skills-unavailable`).
- `docs:write` is a curated capability slot that `fgos setup` declares next to `code:implement`.
- Ctrl-C (or SIGTERM) on `fgos run` stops the attempts it handed over by name: the controller asks each supervisor to cancel, waits for the receipts for at most `dispatch.cancelWaitMs`, prints `unit <id> chờ resume: fgos run --resume <id>` and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM); a second signal exits at once and the attempts still end `cancelled`. Config key `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (default `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` + 5000, at least 1000), read by the same project-over-global reader as the kill grace; `fgos setup` does not write it.
- `fgos dispatch inspect`, `dispatch show-run` and `fgos run --json` report `attemptState` and `unitState`; a unit whose controller is gone and whose last attempt is closed reads `awaiting-resume` and names `fgos run --resume <unit>`.
- `fgos dispatch recover` over an attempt of the run supervisor recommends `adopt`.
- `fgos doctor` checks `legacy-attempts-stuck` (runs from before the run supervisor still `running`; `--fix` settles them as `abandoned-legacy` only when every process they recorded is dead and no version-1 home is left, and names the reason for each run it keeps), `units-awaiting-resume` (lists the units to resume, never fails) and `cancel-wait` (`dispatch.cancelWaitMs` and its source; fails below 1000 ms or below `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs`).
- Terminal-control lays panes out from the real size of the tab (`measured-split`): it splits the pane whose smaller half stays largest, and opens a new tab of the same group when no split keeps a pane of at least `terminal.layout.minCols` x `minRows` or the tab holds `maxPanesPerTab`.
- Config section `terminal` (setup adds it when missing): `allocationGraceMs` (60000, the ready timeout plus 30 s at least), `retainFailedPaneMs` (`null`: keep a failed pane until a person closes it), `layout.policy` (`measured-split`), `layout.minCols` (80), `layout.minRows` (20), `layout.maxPanesPerTab` (8). Project over global over default. `fgos setup` also creates `<stateRoot>/terminal` (mode 0700). No new environment variable.
- `fgos doctor` checks `terminal-control` (driver, declared capabilities and herdr server incarnation; a missing herdr is a warning and says direct mode is unaffected; a bad `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` fails), `terminal-config` (each `terminal.*` value with its source; fails by name on a rule it breaks) and `terminal-allocations` (slots stuck past the grace and retained panes past their time; reports only, closes nothing).
- `herdr-spawn` rounds, the account probe and the confinement reaper now reach herdr only through terminal-control. Panes of one batch (a coding panel, or the attempts of one unit run) share one tab labeled with the batch key, and the first worker's own pane opens the tab, so no empty root pane is left and fgOS never closes a tab. A pane kept for a person after a failed round stays open and can be closed by its slot key (`terminalKey` in `visibility.json`); a confined home written by an older release names no slot, so its pane is not closed on a guess. The `fgos-lead-<key>-<ts>` tab labels are gone. Needs a host with the `fgos internal terminal-control` route (an activated release built from this source, or `FGOS_HOST_BIN`).
- Windows now has a holder-lock driver (`LockFileEx` in the locking process; Node holds a lock through one `fgos internal lock-hold` helper per lock). The gateway, sessions, runner, dispatch, advance, recovery, the provider locks, `fgctl` activation and observe all take their kernel locks on Windows, so `fgos run` no longer refuses there with `lock-driver-unavailable`. A git child that borrows a lock runs in a named job that ends with the borrow. `fgos doctor` reports `lockfileex`/`kernel`, and the borrow vectors and the `fgctl` activation gate run on Windows. A crash during a borrowed git commit costs about 120-170 ms at the next acquire. A `windows-job` predecessor record is judged by the host (`fgos internal lock-fd --predecessor-state`, read-only), and `lock-holders` warns with the domain and the reason when it is not empty.
- `fgos dispatch explain --for <capability> [--rigor <r>]` shows why a capability runs where it does, without running anything: the family and the `prefer` entry that chose it, the tier and where it came from (rigor, override, `maxTier`), the whole `modelPolicies` cell with the entry that runs, the executor and invocation, and the accounts of the family's pool in `runner.providers` and `runner.llmAccounts`.
- `fgos doctor` checks for the model, pool and account config: `executor-family-unique` (two agent executors of one family fail), `model-policy-pools` (a `model@pool` cell entry whose pool `runner.llmAccounts` does not declare warns), `llm-accounts-shape` (a malformed `runner.llmAccounts`, or one in the project config, fails), `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` (once `runner.llmAccounts` is declared, accounts or login directories that differ from `runner.providers` warn; the lease still reads `runner.providers`) and `global-model-policies-portable` (a list or `model@pool` cell in `~/.fgos/config.json` fails).
- A `runner.modelPolicies.<family>.<tier>` cell in the project config may name the pool that serves the model (`model@pool`, split at the last `@`) or list several in order (`["deepseek-v4@openrouter", "deepseek-v4"]`). A run uses the first entry served by the family's own pool (an entry without `@`); entries for other pools are accepted and wait for pool routing. The global `~/.fgos/config.json` keeps plain strings only: a list or `@` cell there is ignored with a warning, because older fgOS releases on the machine cannot read it. A cell with no entry for the family's pool counts as a missing tier.
- `fgos doctor` checks for holder-lock, the kernel locks behind gateway, sessions, runner, dispatch and the provider accounts: `lock-kernel-semantics` (both lock directories give kernel exclusion, proven by a two-process probe; a network filesystem and a platform with no lock driver fail by name; on Windows it reports `lockfileex`/`kernel`), `lock-borrow-vectors` (a lock lent to a git child never leaks to a background process; red fails), `lock-holders` (warns on a holder that is not a fgOS process, and on a previous holder's processes still running), `lock-fences` (warns while a legacy lock path has no cutover fence), `lock-predecessor-kill-wait` and `state-root` (Node and the host resolve the same state root).
- `fgos doctor` check `lock-record-unreadable` warns when the `state` or `porting-events` hot record in `.fgos/locks/` does not parse, or names a holder the judge cannot place for more than five minutes; it names the file and `fgos lock fence <name>`, and never fixes by itself.
- On Windows the `state` and `porting-events` hot locks now reclaim a crashed holder like on Linux: the holder's creation time is read through the new host route `fgos internal process-observe`, so a dead holder's record is cleaned within the five second wait and a live one never is; an unopenable holder or a host that cannot be run still fails closed (`fgos lock fence`).
- On Windows a borrowed git child and the job keeper no longer inherit the handles the lock holder owns: they are started with an explicit inherited-handle list holding only their own standard streams.
- Config key `lock.predecessorKillWaitMs` (default 2000 ms, 1 to 60000): the longest wait, after the processes a dead lock holder left are killed, for them to exit before the lock goes to the next holder. `fgos setup` adds it and creates `.fgos/locks` and `~/.local/state/fgos/locks` (mode 0700).
