- `fgos doctor --fix` (and `fgos setup`) places the cutover fences once the workspace's activated release runs holder-lock and no other fgOS process of the workspace is running; it lists the processes still running instead of placing anything. Activate this release in every workspace first, then fence.
- `fgctl` refuses to activate a release when the holder-lock semantics probe or the borrow vectors are red on this machine (`lock-kernel-semantics-failed`, `lock-borrow-vectors-failed`); the gate runs on Windows too, and a platform with no lock driver refuses with `lock-kernel-semantics-failed`.
- New skill `instruction-audit` (`/instruction-audit`) audits any repository's agent instruction surface on demand or on a schedule. It measures what each agent runtime (Claude Code, AGENTS.md readers, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot) loads on every turn, finds blocks loaded twice and which tool wrote them, duplicate or broken hook registrations, and paths in settings that no longer exist. It also runs read-only lanes over rules, enforcement and git history, and writes a ranked report with a delta against the previous run. It never edits the files it audits.
- `fgos identity [--pid <n>] [--fgos-dir <dir>]` prints which writer the calling process is, as `{id, source}`. The answer comes from one place, the Rust crate `fgos-session-identity`, which Node now calls for every state write; `fgos doctor` check `writer-identity-resolvable` asks both the running host and the activated release (the one a plain `git commit` hook uses).
- `fgos workflow start` supports `--timeout <dur>` and `--account <id>` flags, propagating overrides down to each Unit run while honoring Unit self-declared timeouts.
- `fgos doctor` check `executor-posture-coverage` verifies that core capabilities have executors capable of applying required posture, providing actionable remediation instructions when misconfigured.
- `fgos run --timeout <dur>` (for example `90m` or `5400s`, from 1m to 4h), a `"timeoutMs"` key in `--override`, or a Unit's own `timeoutMs` (also in a units file) gives one run more (or less) time than `runner.timeoutMs`. The value is kept for resume (`--timeout` is refused with `--resume`). A run longer than an hour no longer has its private home reclaimed mid-turn, and a dispatch with a shorter timeout no longer takes the worktree lock of a longer run. `runner.timeoutMs` above 4h is now refused.
- `fgos run --sync <ref>` (Unit field `syncBase`) merges a branch into the worktree's branch before the worker runs: the runner runs the merge and commits it, so a confined worker never needs git. A clean merge is committed as `chore(sync): merge <ref>`; on conflicts the conflicted files join the write scope and the worker's brief, and the runner concludes the merge commit after a passing round, refusing while a conflict marker is left (`fgos run --resume` then commits once they are gone). `--sync <ref> --writes <paths>` without a prompt only syncs. A sync never takes the base's changes under `.fgos/` (the branch keeps its own), and a pre-commit hook that refuses the merge commit is reported as `hook-refused` with the hook's message.
- `fgos doctor`'s `workflow-capabilities-configured` also warns when `code:implement`, the capability the runner loop's coding executing step asks for, has no `prefer` pool.
- `fgos run --effort low|medium|high|max` (or `"reasoningEffort"` in `--override`) sets how hard the worker reasons for one run, without editing the provider's own config. claude and agy get `--effort`, pi and omp `--thinking`, Codex `-c model_reasoning_effort=` (`max` becomes `xhigh`). A level outside that list, or one the bound executor's `supports.reasoningEffort` does not declare, is refused before the worker starts (`fgos run` reports a `policy-refusal` with reason `reasoning-effort`). Until now a derived effort was recorded in the policy but never reached the CLI; that is unchanged when no effort is given.
- A run's result records where the model that ran differs from the one bound, under `policy.provenance.modelDrift`: replaced by policy before launch (`model-overridden`), not passed on the command line (`model-not-passed`), refused or unknown to the provider CLI (`model-unsupported`), or reported differently by the CLI (`model-reported-different`).
- `fgos run "<prompt>"` runs a one-line task as a Unit. The flags are `--provider` (soft preference), `--persona`, `--writes` (needs a linked worktree), `--capability` (default `execute`), `--rigor`, `--effort` and `--override`. Without `--writes` the Unit is read-only. A wrong provider, a wrong persona, or writes from the main checkout fail before anything runs.
- `fgos workflow start --units <file>` (a YAML/JSON list of Units) runs the list as a one-off Workflow, one step per Unit. A Unit may carry `prefer` (soft preference) and `persona`; `--units` does not combine with `--seats`.
- `fgos workflow start --effort <level>` asks the same reasoning effort for every unit of the run, kept across resume.
- A Unit may declare `prefer` (a soft executor preference) and `persona`. Its `prefer` goes ahead of the capability's pool, passing the same filters and failing over into the pool; its `persona` binds unless an override names one. Binding provenance records `unit-prefer` / `unit` as the source.
- `fgos run --resume` after a failed runner commit only commits again; the agent does not run a second time. A stray commit holding files outside the write scope blocks the resume until it is taken off the branch (`git reset HEAD~1`).
- Config key `runner.generatedPaths` and doctor check `runner-generated-paths`: a Unit that edits a generated source (for example `core/skills/**`) gets the rendered copies in its write scope too.
- `agent-result.json` takes an optional `needsWrites`: paths the worker needed outside its write scope and did not write.
- `fgos run --account <id>` (or `"account"` in `--override`) pins the provider account: each seat whose bound executor's provider lists that account runs on it, through the normal lease. A pin no seat can take, or an account that is quarantined (the message says until when), is refused before anything runs, and a resume is refused while the pinned account is quarantined. A provider limit on a pinned account ends the seat instead of switching account or executor. Pair it with `--provider` to choose the executor.
- A writing seat that already changed the worktree when it hit a provider limit is no longer run again on another account or executor on top of that half-done work: the unit stops as `provider-limit` with `fallbackExhausted.reason: "partial-writes"` and the changed paths. Read-only seats, and seats that changed nothing, rotate as before.
- `fgos --help --json` and `fgos <verb> [<sub>] --help --json` work through the installed `fgos` in any project: `--help` and `-h` are routed to the verb manifest, `<verb> <sub> --help --json` narrows to one sub-verb, and a Rust-native verb (`version`, `metrics`, `friction`, `convention`, `gate-bypass`) given `--help` prints its manifest entry instead of running. Verbs with sub-verbs (`dispatch`, `workflow`, `merge`, `session`, `gateway`, `goal`, `tool`, `agents`, `metrics`, `friction`, `convention`) list each sub-verb's flags, required fields and examples under `subcommands`.
- `fgctl upgrade` resolves its target release by `--from <path | URL>` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION=<tag>` > the latest GitHub release, verifies a downloaded archive against `SHA256SUMS` before staging, and records the downloaded tag in `.fgos/distribution.json` (`projectRuntime.releaseVersion`) so teammates can acquire the upgraded release via plain `fgctl init`.
- `fgos run` direct attempts are owned by a Rust run supervisor and a gate that is pid 1 of the attempt's process domain (Linux: bwrap PID namespace, or a process group where user namespaces are off; Windows: a Job Object; macOS: a process group tree, best-effort). A controller that dies or is killed no longer loses the CLI's result: the agent keeps running to its deadline, the receipt is written, and the next `fgos run`, runner loop, `dispatch` or `fgos doctor --fix` settles the attempt through `fgos internal adopt`. A supervisor that never started (on Windows, an attempt lock it could not take) is reported with its reason (`start-refused:lock-held`), not only in `supervisor.log`.
- `fgos doctor` checks for the run supervisor: `process-containment` (the driver agents run in and its level, `kernel` or `best-effort`, with the routes around it; a Linux machine with no user namespace warns and never fails), `run-supervisor-route` (the host serves `supervise`, `gate`, `adopt` and `attempt-step` at protocol 1), `runtime-socket-dir` (exists, 0700, yours; setup and `--fix` create it), `run-attempts-stuck` (an attempt with no holder and no `closed.json`; `--fix` adopts it) and `gate-kill-grace`. `lock-holders` counts a bwrap monitor under an attempt's supervisor as a member of the attempt.
- A herdr round now survives the death of the process that started it. The run supervisor watches the pane (deadline, idle, cancel, the pane itself), types the brief, reads the result, settles, and closes the pane for a clean end; a controller that is killed, a supervisor that is killed after the brief (the agent runs on and its result is still settled) and a pane that disappears (the attempt ends as `carrier-lost`) each end with a named outcome and no pane left behind. A pane that stops answering is blind time, never idle time. A finished attempt closes its pane once; any other end keeps it (24 hours by default, `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs`).
- A worker started by `fgos run` now writes under its own writer id, `att-<attemptId>`, in a pane and headless alike: `FGOS_SESSION_ID` is that id, the controller's `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID` and parent `FGOS_PARENT_WRITER_ID` never reach the worker, and `FGOS_PARENT_WRITER_ID` names the controller's writer id. A command run by codex under its shared daemon sees the attempt id only because the codex launch now carries `-c shell_environment_policy.set={FGOS_SESSION_ID="..."}`.
- `fgos doctor` check `runtime-socket-dir` also reports attempt sockets that no supervisor holds any more (a supervisor killed before it could remove its socket); `fgos doctor --fix` removes only those socket files. `run-attempts-stuck` covers panes as well as headless attempts.
- Config key `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` (default 10000 ms, at least 1000): the wait between SIGTERM and SIGKILL when the gate stops an agent. Project config overrides global; `fgos setup` does not write it.

### Changed
- A reviewed run's verify step now runs the Unit's own `verify` (or its capability's) through the bounded command runner, for at most `runner.timeoutMs`, and a failure or a timeout becomes findings that say which; the `code-change` preset no longer pins `npm test` (it was never executed), and a reviewed run with no verify command reports `verify: { ran: false }` in its result instead of passing silently.
- At rigor `high` or `critical`, every seat of a `reviewed` run (producer and each checker) must run on its own provider family; a pool without enough families refuses the seat with reason `independence`. `panel` keeps its soft spread.
- The `/fgOS:cook` slash command is now `/fgOS:deliver` (skill `plugins/fgOS/skills/deliver/`): same behavior, freeing the name `cook` for the orchestration skill planned next. `fgos-coding-driving` names it as a caller, and the shared coordination-driver fragment no longer teaches the removed `fgos coordination` verbs.
- `fgos run --resume` after a controller death no longer runs the agent again: the last attempt is taken through adopt and a settled result is used as it is (the unit carries on to commit, reviewer and summary). A `cancelled` or abandoned attempt is replaced by a new one that names it in `supersedesRunId`; an attempt still running is refused (`attempt-still-running`), and a second `--resume` of the same unit at the same time is refused (`resume-in-progress`). A unit never resumes on its own.
- `herdr-spawn` no longer runs a round loop in the controller. The seat goes through the same door as a headless one (attempt lock, envelope, supervisor), so a herdr seat cannot be started directly any more (`herdr-spawn-supervised-only`). On Windows, and where herdr is not usable, a pane attempt is refused with `terminal-mode-unsupported` and never changes to headless by itself; headless runs are unaffected.
- The confinement orphan reaper is gone. A private home belongs to its attempt and only adopt's finalize-home step removes it, while the attempt's lock is free and its process domain is empty; no sweep judges a home by a pid, a pane or an age any more. `fgos run` start, the runner loop start and `fgos doctor --fix` now only finish unfinished attempts. A herdr-spawn launch without a supervised attempt is refused (`attempt-required`), `fgos dispatch probe-account` no longer sweeps after closing panes, and the doctor check `confinement-orphaned-resources-reaped` now only tightens root modes, removes empty per-dispatch directories and `--fix` removes a home left by a dead dispatch outside the assignment door (judged by its pid alone, only on that explicit fix). Homes written by an older release with a pane binding are not reaped by this release: remove them with the previous release's `fgos run` before activating.
- The Git component spec (`fgos-git`, `docs/platform/git/spec.md`) is accepted: it is the single owner of every fgOS git mutation (commits, merges and land, worktrees, refs, fetch and push, and the publication of `refs/fgos/*` for the Event Store), and Workflow, Execution, Work, Event Store and setup become its consumers. No behavior changes yet; today's git writers stay until the Git plan replaces them.
- Doctor check `herdr-available` is replaced by `terminal-control`, which asks the terminal port instead of running `herdr --version` itself and keeps the `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` diagnosis. A machine without herdr now gets a warning, not a failure.
- A later step of one run whose earlier tab already closed itself opens a new tab with the same label instead of failing to find the old one.
- Windows: every terminal operation answers `unsupported` until herdr ships a Windows build; doctor says so, and direct (headless) mode is unaffected.
- `fgos unlock` is removed; the verb now answers `unknown verb "unlock"`, and the `/fgOS:unlock` command is gone. A held repo lock always has a live holder (kernel lock, no TTL, no stale record), so there is nothing to clear: wait, or stop a wedged holder with `fgos lock fence <name> [--param k=v] [--yes] [--attest-stopped]`. It lists the holders (pid, start time, command line), asks for confirmation, sends SIGTERM by identity, waits 5 s, sends SIGKILL, and checks with a probe that the lock is free; it never takes a lock from a live holder, and where holders cannot be listed `--attest-stopped` only re-checks. The skill `fgos-unlock` is now `fgos-lock-fence`.
- `fgos lock-status --json` reports every repo and machine lock of the registry as `free` or `held` (`locks`, with holder pids and the filesystem guarantee); the main checkout lock is under `mainCheckout` (`outcome` is `free` or `held`, `holders` replaces `holderPid`; `lockAge`, `remainingTtl` and `live`/`stale`/`ambiguous` are gone) and the commit-activity beacon moved from `activity` to `beacon`.
- `fgos main-checkout-reset` runs while holding the main checkout lock; with another process holding it the verb refuses at once with `lock-timeout`, naming the lock and the holder pid, and touches nothing. `fgos take`/`pick` wait for the main checkout lock as before (`--wait`, `--no-wait`).
- `.fgos/locks/*.lock` files never count as a change in an item's own footprint at `fgos return`.
- The main checkout lock, the merge slot of each target ref and the new `worktree-admin` lock (around every `git worktree add`) are kernel locks taken through one door (`src/runner/repo-locks.mjs`): no TTL, no ambiguous state, no recognition of a holder by pid, and a holder that dies releases at once. A git child of a checkpoint or merge, and the pre-commit hook it runs, act under the lock because they inherit the locked file description (`FGOS_LOCK_FD`); `FGOS_MAIN_LOCK_HOLDER_PID` is gone. A claim holds the main checkout lock through its `.fgos` checkpoint, worker-slot check and claim record, and creates its `--isolate` worktree after releasing it.
- `fgos doctor --fix` (with every fgOS process stopped) also fences the old main checkout lock and one old merge slot per local branch with a `TOMBSTONE` directory at `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` and `.fgos/merge-slot--<ref>.lock`. A release from before this change that meets one fails with `EISDIR`, and its pre-commit hook refuses a commit on the main checkout; rolling back to it is by hand: remove those `TOMBSTONE` directories. The `lock-holders` and `lock-fences` doctor checks now cover these locks; a branch created after the fences were placed needs `fgos doctor --fix` once more for its slot.
- The state store takes one hot mutex per clone, `state` (work events, claims and the state view, replacing `.fgos/events.lock` and `.fgos/runtime/claims.lock`) or `porting-events` (replacing `.fgos/porting/events.lock`), through `withStateTx`: the record is `.fgos/locks/<resource>.hot`, a dead holder is cleaned only under a kernel lock, and the wait is 5 s. A claim checks the worker-slot ceiling in the same transaction as the claim record and takes the main checkout lock only around the `.fgos` checkpoint commit. `FGOS_EVENTS_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` is gone.
- Starting a subprocess inside a state transaction, or taking a state mutex again while holding one, throws `exec-under-hot-lock` / `hot-lock-reentry` at once. On Windows a hot record is never cleaned (no dead-holder judge yet): a stuck one is cleared with `fgos lock fence state`.
- A record that does not parse, or whose holder cannot be judged, is never cleaned: the waiter times out with `lock-record-unreadable`, and a person who confirmed the holder is gone runs `fgos lock fence state` (or `porting-events`).
- `fgos doctor --fix` (with every fgOS process stopped) also fences the three old state locks with a `TOMBSTONE` directory at `.fgos/events.lock`, `.fgos/runtime/claims.lock` and `.fgos/porting/events.lock`. A release from before this change that reaches any of them stops with a raw `EISDIR` (measured with the real old `withEventsLock` and `withClaimsLock`).
- `runner.maxTier` no longer holds down a capability that declares a higher `rigor` itself in `runner.capabilities`: its seats run up to that rigor's tier (with the committed config, `architecture:synthesize`, `architecture:shape` and `architecture:explain` now run at `frontier`). A unit's rigor and a tier override still stop at `runner.maxTier`. `fgos doctor` check `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted this way and the model they run.
- Each agent family now has one executor. The `claude-herdr` executor is merged into `claude` (its pane invocation `claude-herdr-bwrap` moves there), and `glm-herdr` is removed (GLM runs headless through OpenRouter only). The 26 capabilities that named `claude-herdr` now name `claude`, so they run claude both inside herdr (in a pane) and headless; before, headless they fell over to codex, gemini or xai. Replace `--provider claude-herdr` with `--provider claude`.
- Agents now receive the full locked law list L1-L10 (L9 and L10 were missing from the projected instructions) and a new instruction unit, `core/instructions/design-principles.md`, with seven design principles (one door, bottom-up layering, thin drivers behind ports, Rust-first foundations, correctness first, KISS/DRY, one authority per decision). The coding worker contract and `fgos-coding-implement` now require searching the whole repository for an existing mechanism before adding a new one, importing the shared module an import guard names instead of copying code, and deleting the old path in the same change when replacing a mechanism.
- Every `fgos` verb now refuses a flag its registry entry does not declare: exit 4, `unknown flag "--x" for "fgos <verb>"` plus the verb's valid flags and a pointer to `--help`, instead of silently ignoring a typo that could make a command do something else. One check serves both doors: the legacy-node payload reads `src/cli/command-registry.mjs`, and the Rust host reads the same flag lists projected into `command-routes.json` (`accepted_flags` / `subcommand_flags`, regenerate with `node scripts/export-command-selectors.mjs`). `--dir`, `--json` and `--help` are accepted everywhere; the `--name=value` form is not accepted by the legacy-node verbs (write `--name value`). Flags the handlers already read but the registry never listed are now declared (for example `--worktree`, `--trust-dir`, `--no-timeout`, `--stance-options`, `--runtime-json`), so they show up in `fgos <verb> --help --json`.
- `fgctl init`, `upgrade` and `repair` decide on the main checkout only by probing its kernel lock; the old `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` file (a live pid, a session id, an unparseable record or a tombstone) is no longer read, and the `lock-ambiguous` and `lock-unsupported` refusals are gone.
- The `fgctl` activation lock, the machine install lock and the Observe store lock are kernel locks (`<fgosDir>/locks/activation.lock`, `<stateRoot>/locks/install.lock`, `<fgosDir>/locks/observe.lock`): no TTL, no stale reclaim, and a killed holder frees the lock at once, so there is no 3-minute activation or 30-second Observe expiry to wait out and no stuck `install.lock` to delete by hand (the Observe lock waits 5 s and writes its shard snapshot under the lock). `.fgos/installation/activation.lock`, `<stateRoot>/install.lock` and `.fgos/observe/.lock` become tombstone directories, so an older `fgctl` or `fgos` stops with an error there. `fgos doctor --fix` places those three fences only once the workspace's activated release is the one that takes them as kernel locks, so an older `fgctl` can still upgrade the workspace first. On Windows these locks work like elsewhere through the Windows lock driver.
- Gateway, sessions and runner locks are kernel locks in `.fgos/locks/`; a dead holder releases at once. An older release meets a `TOMBSTONE` directory at `.fgos/{gateway,sessions,runner}.lock` and fails with `EISDIR`.
- The full-suite queue is a machine-wide kernel lock at `~/.local/state/fgos/locks/full-suite.lock`, replacing the `/tmp` lock file and its stale-lock reclaim. Branches created before this change keep the old `/tmp` queue and do not queue with newer ones. `npm test` resolves the host binary first (`FGOS_HOST_BIN`, else it builds one with cargo) and then takes the queue; without a host binary it stops with `lock-driver-unavailable`, and `FGOS_FULL_SUITE_QUEUE=off` runs unqueued.
- The provider account locks and the provider-capacity state lock are kernel locks per machine (no longer per runtime directory); the generation directories no longer grow. An older release sees "held by pid 1" on these locks.
- The per-worktree dispatch lock is a kernel lock (still per `.fgos`), keyed by the directory's identity, so a worktree reached through a symlink is the same lock; a dead holder releases it at once and no orphaned `dispatch--*.lock` file blocks a resume any more. A live dispatcher that hangs keeps its worktree locked until it exits. `reconcile.lock` is a kernel lock at `.fgos/locks/reconcile.lock`, and `fgos dispatch reconcile clear-cwd-lock` now only reports whether the lock is held.
- The Rust host sets `FGOS_STATE_ROOT` for the Node payload, and dispatch pins it into every child, so a sandbox HOME does not move the state root. The npm package ships the lock registry `packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json`.
- Taking locks out of order inside one lock scope throws `lock-order-violation` at once. Each lock door takes its own scope today, so locks taken through different doors are not yet checked against each other.
- An older fgOS release run against a fenced workspace fails at its first lock (`EISDIR`, `lock-busy`, `already being advanced`, or a provider lock held by pid 1). Never delete a `TOMBSTONE` directory or a pid-1 generation by hand, unless rolling back to a release from before this one.
- Writer ids change, so settle or release every open claim with the old release before activating this one: `CODEX_THREAD_ID` now identifies a Codex pane (it ranks after `FGOS_SESSION_ID` and before `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`); a bare shell, agy, pi or omp pane resolves to its pane's root shell (the highest ancestor holding a terminal) instead of the herdr server or the CLI's own pid; a process with no terminal above it resolves to its session id.
- Every state write now needs the Rust host binary to name its writer: through the `fgos` command it is always there; `node bin/fgos.mjs` and the npm global `fgos` find it from the project's activation or `FGOS_HOST_BIN`, and otherwise stop with a clear `precondition` error instead of guessing. A commit at the main checkout between merging this change and activating it is refused with `host-version-mismatch` until the release is activated.
- Observe names writer shards (`.fgos/observe/<store>/<writer>.jsonl`) and friction `sessionId` from the same identity: a Claude or Codex session writes under its session id, and every command from one terminal pane shares `pid-<pane root>` instead of one shard per process.
- A runtime claim can now be released only by the writer that took it, the same rule a settle already follows. Another writer is refused with `releaseClaim: writer identity mismatch for "<id>" ...` and the claim stays in place; a parent or lineage id grants nothing. The stale-claim reclaim in `pick` and `fgos unclaim` still clear another session's dead or orphaned claim, and `fgos unclaim` output then carries `admin: {reason, ownerWriterId, releasedByWriterId}`.
- `fgos run` and `fgos workflow start|resume|answer --foreground` now exit with distinctive non-zero exit codes for non-pass outcomes (`policy-refusal`: 4, `provider-limit`: 10, `execution-failure`: 11, `partial-writes`: 12, `blocked`: 13, `findings`: 14; 0 on `pass`) while preserving the structured JSON envelope `fgos.v1` (RUL99). Read-only commands like `fgos workflow status` exit 0.
- `herdr-spawn` now defaults `promptDelivery` to `"inline"` (typing the full rendered brief directly into the pane via bracketed paste while still writing `brief-<round>.md` to disk with a recovery pointer), so a person watching the pane sees the task prompt in the TUI conversation; `"file-pointer"` remains supported per invocation or via `FGOS_HERDR_PROMPT_DELIVERY=file-pointer`. `confirmBriefSubmitted` now detects collapsed TUI paste chips (`[Pasted text #1 +N lines]`, `[paste #1 +N lines]`, `[Paste]`, `#1 … +N lines`, and OMP's `Pasted N lines` modal menu) in `promptText` and the bottom composer lines of the visible screen, `workerBaseEnv` and `SHELL_MANAGED_ENV` preserve the pane's own `TERM`/`HERDR_PANE_ID` and strip parent `OMPCODE`/`OMP_PROFILE`/`PI_PROFILE`/`PI_CONFIG_FILES`, and `executors.xai` gains the confined `omp-herdr-vantt` pane invocation.
- `fgos dispatch decide --work <id>` hands dispatch a hint built by the Work layer (the step's executor, the item's agent type, its rigor with `risk: heavy` read as `high`, and its domain) instead of the item itself; it resolves the same executor and mechanism as before. Dispatch's own functions (`buildAssignment`, `compileDispatchPlan`, `decideExecutorCli`, `executeExecutorCli`, `executeAssignment`, the assignment policy) now refuse a `work`/`workItem` input with "takes no Work item" instead of silently ignoring it, and name the `--work` selector `workId`.
- When the config sets a rigor on a `<domain>:review` capability, a declared assignment of that domain (including a Work driver step) gets that floor: the policy reads the domain the assignment carries. It only ever raises rigor.
- Dispatch no longer imports a domain's contract harness (`domains/<d>/harness/enrich-and-validate-contract.mjs`) by a computed path; only the Work layer loads it, for a caller to hand in.
- The runner loop (`fgos-runner`) and the fan-out batch run each worker as one Unit run, through the same boundary as `fgos run`: the worker runs confined and never commits, and the runner commits what it left. The item's log names the Unit run (`unitRunId`) and where its output is captured instead of teeing the worker's output live, and the `executor.dispatch` event carries `unitRunId`. Commit subjects become `chore(work-<id>-<step>): <the worker's claim summary>`.
- A runner loop step asks for its capability as `<domain>:<verb>` (for example `coding:discover`), the name its Workflow uses; a config that only declares the bare verb still serves it.
- An item no executor can run (its capability has no usable pool) parks as `no-executor`, with the pool to configure in the message, instead of stopping the runner. Every candidate at its provider limit parks the item as `provider-limit`. A worker round that fails after writing files is `worker-failed`: retried, and its uncommitted files are never verified as if they were on the branch.
- A runner loop round that stopped over its own half-done writes, or whose runner commit failed, keeps its worktree; the item's next attempt resumes the same Unit run there, committing again without running the agent a second time.
- Driver steps of a work item (`fgos plan <id> --validate`, and the runner loop's validate-plan, review and scout operations) run as Units through the same door as `fgos run`. Their worker is confined, so a read-only operation can no longer write to the checkout. A step stops instead of advancing when its runner commit failed. Results recorded before this change are still read.
- A validate-plan verdict is bound to the bytes of `plan.md`, keyed by its path inside the checkout. A plan validated in the item worktree and merged byte for byte is therefore not validated again, and any edit after validation still forces a new one.
- Driver steps need a confinement backend (bwrap). Without one, the step stops with `unit-refused-posture-unavailable` instead of running unconfined.
- An item with `rigor: low` that runs as a Unit uses the `standard` tier.
- Resuming a unit run uses the pattern it started with; a pattern passed on resume is ignored.
- A runner commit whose worker left no summary is named after the goal line of the unit's objective instead of `producer changes`. A long commit subject is cut at a sentence or word boundary instead of ending in `...`.
- `fgos run` (and a Workflow unit) commits only files inside the Unit's `writes`. Files outside it are left in place and reported in `commit.outOfScope`; files you were already editing inside the scope are left as they are (`preExistingInScope`).
- The runner refuses to start a writing Unit while the index already holds staged changes (`foreign-staged-index`); unstage or commit them and run again.
- Runner commits use a conventional subject: the first line of the worker's `summary`, or `chore(<unitId>): …` when that is not conventional.
- Unit `writes` are normalized to one spelling and `.`, absolute paths, `..` and pathspec magic `:` are refused; only `*` and `**` are globs.
- A Workflow definition's `writes` must be a list: an empty `writes:` in YAML (null) or any other non-list value is refused instead of silently becoming `[]`.
- A writing seat of a unit run is told its write scope, that the runner (not the agent) commits, that the commit subject comes from the first line of `summary`, and to declare `needsWrites` when it needs a path outside the scope.
- A unit run's evidence marks files inside the declared `writes` (`coverageMatched`) and warns about files outside them.
- A `persona` in a workflow unit template travels on the Unit (provenance `unit`) instead of becoming an `origin: workflow` override.
- A writing workflow unit that depends on another writing unit now starts from that unit's branch instead of HEAD; `workflow status` lists `writeBranches`.
- A writing unit that changed files outside its `writes` ends as `findings`; an integrate step that meets such a unit fails and merges nothing (it used to skip it silently).
- A writing unit that cannot get a worktree of its own now fails instead of running in the shared checkout.
- The verb manifest's `schema_version` is `3.0`: a verb with sub-verbs keeps only `sub` in its verb-level `parameters`, and each sub-verb's flags are under `subcommands.<sub>.parameters`.
- `fgos --help` refuses an unknown verb, sub-verb, extra word or option with exit 4 instead of ignoring it. It still accepts `--dir`, which the `fgos` shell function appends.
- The `fgos run` and `fgos workflow` help say which door to use: one task → `fgos run "<prompt>"`; planned work → `fgos workflow start <preset>|--units <file>`.
- A fresh checkout, a linked worktree and `fgos setup` no longer need `npm install`: fgOS has no npm runtime dependency now. Its YAML parser (js-yaml) ships inside the source tree and every YAML read goes through one wrapper, `src/util/yaml.mjs`, so `fgos doctor` check `dependencies-installed` passes with "no runtime dependencies declared" and the workflow tests load without `node_modules`.
- Agent definitions (`fgos/agents`, `domains/*/agents`, `core/agents`) and project or domain workflow files must be valid YAML. `fgos doctor` names a file that is not, with its line and column, in the checks `agent-claims-resolve`, `agent-type-names-unique`, `workflow-capabilities-configured`, `workflow-pools-satisfy-independence` and `blind-steps-use-proven-pools`; a seat that names such a definition is refused, and the agent roster skips it with one warning line on stderr. A definition indented as a whole now reads as a mapping and seats; a numeric `name: 123` reads as "123".
- `fgos doctor` checks `workflow-pools-satisfy-independence` and `blind-steps-use-proven-pools` now evaluate in a copy without dependencies instead of passing with "not evaluated", so a project can see new failures there. A workflow that cannot be parsed fails those checks and `workflow-capabilities-configured` by name, but no longer hides their results for the other workflows. A problem path is prefixed `package:` or `project:` when both trees are scanned, and a file that cannot be read is reported as such rather than as unparsable.
- A persona whose list item or value reads as a mapping (an unquoted `": "`, for example `- Escalate when: budget exceeded`) is refused with its path by `fgos agents`, `fgos doctor` and persona resolution, instead of the text being dropped silently. Pinned text from an earlier run with that shape still renders as it was pinned.
- A workspace persona that cannot be parsed or has the wrong shape refuses `fgos run` and workflow unit runs with the named problem; before, the run fell back to the core persona of the same name or to no persona text.
- A YAML file whose aliases expand past 100000 values, or that references itself, is rejected with a message naming the file.
- `fgos doctor` check `agent-type-names-unique` reports problems as `<file>: <problem>`, like the other checks. The dispatch warning `agent roster: …` for a bad agent file prints once per process instead of on every lookup.
- `fgos doctor` check `domain-registry-compiled` now also reports a `compiled.json` that is stale against its YAML and domain YAML that cannot be parsed; `npm run build:domains` regenerates it.
- Persona text rendered into a worker prompt now comes from the parsed agent file: a block-scalar value shows in full, an inline `# comment` is stripped and a number is normalised (`1e3` shows as `1000`). A persona file that cannot be parsed renders one `could not be parsed` line instead of silently dropping its section; a run pinned by an earlier release resumes with the persona text it was pinned with.
- The doctor check for orphaned confinement resources skips attempt homes (they belong to adopt) and its fix goes through the same sweep as the other cleanup call sites; it never removes an attempt home.

### Removed
- The controller's herdr round: the polling loop, its deadline and idle handling, the settle and pane-closing code, the launcher script and its process checks, `herdr-reconcile`, the liveness probe and `herdr-diagnosis.json`, and the pane, endpoint and launch-time fields of the home ownership marker. A home written with a pane binding by an older release is no longer swept: clean it with that release before activating this one.

- The Node run supervisor (`detached-run-supervisor.mjs`), its IPC channel to the controller and its pane-less home binding (`bindConfinedHomesToSupervisor`), the old cli-spawn reconciler (`reconcile-cli-spawn.mjs`), the `legacySpawn` option and the `protected/supervisor-binding` and `protected/adapter-receipts` files of cli-spawn runs. Runs started before this release keep their files and are read as `legacy-run`.
- `fgos doctor` check `provider-capacity-lock-stale`: the provider-capacity state is no longer guarded by a lock file a dead process can leave behind.
- `fgos-runner --config <path>`: the runner and its workers always use the repo's own `.fgos/config.json`.
- `fgos dispatch execute` is gone, together with its `--contract` and `--assignment` forms and the `node src/runner/dispatch.mjs execute` alias. Run one task with `fgos run "<prompt>" --provider <executor>` (`--provider` takes an agent executor; a `kind: "tool"` executor is called directly) (add `--writes <paths> --worktree <linked-worktree>` for work that changes files; the runner commits them), or a Unit file with `fgos run --unit <file>`; planned work goes through `fgos workflow start`. Calling the old door returns an error naming the replacement, and the dispatch-decide hook's BLOCKED message names the same `fgos run` form.
- `fgos dispatch log` is gone: every `fgos run` already records its Unit, binding, results and commit under `.fgos/assignments/<unitRunId>/`.
- `dispatch fanout-batch` is gone. Fanout runs from `node src/runner/fanout-batch.mjs "<ids>" [--has-live-task-access]`, with the same output keys (`fired`, `mechanismChanged`, `unavailable`, `deferred`, and `slotsFull: true` when no slot is free).
- `decide --work` runs only as `fgos dispatch decide --work <id>`; `node src/runner/dispatch.mjs decide --work` is refused with a pointer to it.
- `AGENTS.md` and every skill render no longer teach the removed doors. Other projects keep their old rendered skills until they activate a release that carries this change and run `fgos setup`.
- The `yaml` npm dependency, the hand-written YAML readers in the doctor checks and the persona renderer, and the "not evaluated: yaml package not installed" branches. `fgos doctor` no longer warns about multi-line persona markers because they now render.

### Fixed
- `fgos dispatch recover` no longer parks an orphaned attempt only because `outbox/result-N.json` exists, and a unit whose only attempt the legacy sweep settled no longer reads `running`.
- Attempts left `running` with no holder are cleaned up: new ones through adopt (`run-attempts-stuck`), runs from before the run supervisor through `legacy-attempts-stuck`.
- The gate of a supervised attempt can read its envelope and run when the run directory or the host binary lives under `/tmp`: the sandbox mounts its own `/tmp`, so both are now bound back in place. Before, such a run ended `gate-lost` with `envelope unreadable`.
- A `FGOS_HOST_BIN` that names a file that cannot be run is now an error everywhere the host is looked up; it no longer falls back to the activated release.
- A borrowed lock no longer kills unrelated child processes of the lock holder: cleanup kills the borrowed command, its process group and any escaped descendant that still holds the lock, and waits for the holder’s other children that are between fork and exec (Rust and Node use the same rule). A borrow also refuses a lock whose file was replaced (`lock-resource-replaced`).
- Process containment no longer reports `spawn-failed` when a short command exits before its identity is read; a gate that already exited counts as an empty domain.
- A gemini worker now runs the model its tier asks for. Since gemini moved to omp, the omp invocations passed no `--model`, so every tier ran the profile default (`gemini-3.8-flash`); a frontier task now runs `gemini-4-argon`.
- `fgos take`, `fgos list` and every other verb that reads active claims no longer spawn one git process per open claim; with 60 open claims a `take` drops from about 270 child processes and 1.7 s to 21 processes and 0.26 s.

- The advance and recovery locks no longer stay stuck when their holder dies while creating the lock file; both now live under the run's `locks/` directory.
- The `fgos run --resume` guard no longer treats a dispatch lock it cannot read as free.
- `fgos dispatch reconcile` help, usage errors and docs no longer advertise the retired `clear-assignment-claim` action (and its `--assignment` flag); the planner already refused it, so the supported actions are `clear-cwd-lock`, `collect-result` and `repair-projection`.
- The confinement orphan reaper no longer deletes the private home (and the login copy in it) of a worker that is still running when the process that launched it dies. A confined herdr round now records its pane, the herdr socket its client used, its own pid and start time and the time of binding in the home's ownership marker before the worker starts (a round that cannot record this closes its pane and fails), and a cli-spawn round records its detached run supervisor the same way. A home whose recorded process is alive is kept for its run timeout plus launch and settle grace from that moment, whatever herdr answers; a home bound to a pane that never received a worker is removed and the empty pane closed. Panes of default-session rounds can now be asked about, and the reaper re-reads the marker before removing a home, skipping one that changed since it decided.
- `fgos run --provider <executor>` (a bare executor id in a Unit's `prefer`) inside herdr now binds the executor's herdr invocation, as a capability pool does, instead of the confined cli invocation posture approval had filled in (transport source `unit-prefer-pinned-invocation`). A `prefer` entry that names an invocation, or an override's invocation, still keeps it.
- Releasing another writer's runtime claim is now auditable after the claim file is gone: `fgos unclaim` appends a `decision` event (`source: unclaim`, `kind: engine`) with `admin: {reason, ownerWriterId, releasedByWriterId, claimId}`, and the stale-claim reclaim in `pick` adds the same `admin` field to the decision it already wrote. A writer releasing its own claim records nothing new.
- `fgos run --rigor low` (and a Unit's `rigor: low`) now binds the nano tier when the capability declares no `rigor` floor; bind used to treat the implicit `standard` as a floor, so a low run on `execute` resolved `sonnet` instead of the `nano` model. A capability's own `rigor` still raises a lower Unit rigor.
- `/fgOS:terminal` and `/fgOS:terminal-close` act only on the caller's own live herdr pane. Before renaming or closing, they ask herdr for the pane named by `HERDR_PANE_ID` and check that its shell is an ancestor of the caller; a dead pane or another session's pane (the id a shared `codex app-server` daemon passes to every child) is refused with a one-line message on stderr and nothing is changed.
- `fgos dispatch probe-account` no longer removes a private home kept for a pane that is still open once that home is past its maximum age: the sweep it runs after closing its own panes asks herdr about every other pane exactly as the regular sweep does, instead of treating them as unanswerable.
- A cli-spawn `fgos run` whose controlling process crashes or is killed mid-run no longer loses the worker: the detached run supervisor stops sending live output to the dead controller instead of crashing on the closed channel, so the worker keeps running, the deadline is still enforced, and the run's capture and receipt are still written.
- `fgos pick`/`take`, `fgos approve` (land) and `fgctl init` no longer wait up to 3 minutes after every commit on the main checkout, including the committing session's own. The fgOS pre-commit hook no longer writes `.fgos/main-checkout.lock`; it leaves a commit-activity beacon in `.fgos/runtime/main-checkout-activity.json` (writer, time and a `windowMs`, 20 s by default or `FGOS_MAIN_CHECKOUT_LOCK_TTL_MS`) that only the hook reads, to refuse another session's commit inside that window. `fgos lock-status` reports the beacon as `activity`, and `fgos return`/`cleanup`/`compound` clear the session's own beacon instead of the lock. The hook still refuses a commit, without waiting, while an fgOS claim, checkpoint or land holds the lock.
- Every holder of `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` or a merge slot now records its own `ttlMs` (the dispatch worktree lock is a kernel lock with no ttl, see above), and a contender judges the record by that ttl instead of its own (a dispatch with a longer timeout no longer outwaits a shorter holder, and a short contender no longer takes a longer holder's lock). A record left by an older release counts for 20 s when it is a session id (old hook) and 3 minutes when it is a pid.
- The `.fgos` events checkpoint that runs during `fgos approve` under a merge slot now holds `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` for its whole add, commit and reset, so it can no longer interleave with a land on the main checkout; when a land holds the lock the checkpoint is skipped until the next call. Claim and a merge without a slot reuse the lock they already hold.
- A lock record with a `v` field (even one that also has `pid` and `ts`), or a lock protocol marker (`.fgos/runtime/locks/<lock>/protocol.json`) naming any protocol other than 1, is refused with "upgrade fgOS" and is never reclaimed, released, renewed or overwritten by this release. The marker is checked before anything else, so the pre-commit hook, `fgos lock-status`, `fgos unlock`, the claim self-heal and `fgctl init` all refuse even when the lock file itself is absent or corrupt; `fgos unlock` never reports `cleared` there. Do not downgrade below this release once a newer lock protocol is in use.
- A native `fgos` verb that takes no stdin (for example `fgos convention path ...`) no longer waits for an inherited stdin to close: it hung under a heredoc, an agent Bash tool, or a pipe whose writer stays open. Only `metrics ping`, `metrics eval record`, and `friction record --detail-stdin` read stdin.
- A headless round that stops because the provider account used up its quota (codex "You've hit your usage limit") now settles as `provider-limit` with `failure.cause: quota` instead of a generic non-zero exit, so a Workflow unit or `fgos run` moves to another account or candidate, and a leased account waits out the reset time the provider printed.
- A dispatch round is no longer refused because files changed in a shared checkout while it ran (`wrote-outside-workspace`, `read-only-mutation`, `mutated-dirty-before-files`). A before/after snapshot cannot tell the worker's writes from another session's, so the round is accepted and the paths are reported in its result as `warnings` (`stray-write-correlated`, `read-only-mutation-correlated`, `mutated-dirty-before-correlated`) and on stderr. A write proven to be the run's own would still be refused; nothing proves one yet.
- An Assignment run's `result.json` now names the sandbox it really ran under in `confinement` (`bwrap`), read from the launch the Confinement Authority prepared or the dispatch's enforced attestation; it was always `null` before, even for sandboxed seats.
- A Work item stopped on a read-only round whose checkout changed while it ran now says so: the round is accepted with its `warnings`, and the driver stops with `assignment-<operation>-correlated-mutation` (at planning `validation-correlated-mutation-do-not-advance-work`) instead of a generic failed or no-evidence reason. A round launched through the executor CLI door now keeps that door's `stray-write-correlated` warning in its `result.json` instead of only printing it.
- `fgos run --resume` is refused while a live dispatch still holds the worktree's lock, so a second worker is never started in the same worktree; the old guard read a lock name no dispatch writes and never refused.
- A Unit's `persona` is resolved and its text pinned when the unit run starts, so a persona defined only in the workspace (`fgos/agents/`) is rendered with its definition instead of its bare name.
- A help token never runs the verb: `fgos init --json -h` created a store and `fgos session start --json -h` created a worktree, because the help token was read as the previous flag's value; through the Rust host, `fgos version --help` ran `version` and `fgos metrics runs --help` ran `runs`.
- Manifest entries now match what the CLI reads: `merge next` lists the flags it forwards to approve/sync-root, `workflow start --stance-options`, `workflow operations --step` (was `--stage`), `tool --config`, `tool check --name` (was a positional), `dispatch decide --assignment`, `run record --result`. AGENTS.md and the dispatch fallback skill say `decide --work <id> [--stage <stage>]` (was `--step`).
- `fgos main-checkout-reset` without `--confirm` moves forward again in a repository that tracks `.fgos` files: tracked `.fgos` paths that match HEAD are updated with the rest of the tree, and the reset refuses `restore-protected-fgos-path` only while a tracked `.fgos` path differs from HEAD.
- On a host without user namespaces (`linux-pgroup`), a ScopedCommit, Sync or Land whose hook or filter left a `setsid` or double-fork child alive after the borrow now returns `containment-unproven` as `recovery-required` instead of plain success; operations without hooks or filters are unchanged.

### Security

- The runner commit no longer trusts a worktree's `.git` file, a relative hooks path or fsmonitor: its git runs against the main repository's gitdir with the caller's `GIT_*` variables dropped, and a worktree outside the main repository is refused.
- The holder-lock routes (`lock-fd`, `lock-hold`, `state-root`, `process-observe`, `lock-borrow-vectors`) now speak internal protocol 2. A stale global npm `fgos` whose Node payload still sends `--protocol 1` is refused by the new host with `host-version-mismatch` before any lock is taken; reinstall or upgrade the npm package to match the active release. `quiesce-scan` stays on protocol 1.

```txt
Audience: Maintainer, implementation agent, reviewer

Last reviewed: 2026-09-13

Provenance: Existing area document plus source-detail carriage at 77830ba77eb05991d95b005919776ee6254e833b
Writer type: Human + agent coauthor
Canonical for: The topic stated by this document, subject to the unchanged switchboard route and independent review
Use this when: Reading this area topic and its retained design details
Do not use this for: Claiming a truth review or an authority cutover from carriage alone
Supersedes: No authority transition in this carriage pass
Superseded by: None recorded
```

## 1. Purpose

The doctor/fix registry is the extension point for environment readiness. Modules register checks, fixes, and config defaults instead of adding one-off repair logic.

Target architecture has no separate `fgos setup` verb for workspace onboarding. `fgctl init` is the one-command workspace onboarding orchestrator; after activation it invokes active local `fgos init`, `fgos doctor --fix`, and `fgos doctor`. Legacy shell/global integration remains compatibility behavior under the explicit deprecated fallback window: 30 calendar days after preview release publication, unless a later release decision replaces that policy.

Current Node `fgos setup` remains implemented as deprecated legacy compatibility and consumes the same registry while it exists.

## 2. Registry Types

| Registry | Function | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Check | `registerCheck` | A named diagnostic reported by `fgos doctor`. |
| Fix | `registerFix` | A named repair run by `fgos doctor --fix`; current legacy `fgos setup` also runs fixes while it remains implemented. |
| Config default | `registerConfigDefault` | A default config shape merged into shared config without overwriting user values. |

`event-store` registers the `eventStore` config shape `{ remote: "origin" }`. Config merge fills missing keys while preserving explicit remote choices; `git-publication-refspecs` diagnoses and repairs obsolete exact legacy mappings on the configured remote and on historical `origin`.

The registries are independent. A module may register only a check, only a fix, only a config default, or any combination.

## 3. Doctor Contract

`fgos doctor`:

- runs registered checks;
- reports individual pass/fail status;
- does not write files by default;
- should tell the user what command or fix path applies when a check fails.

Run coverage is checked by `observe-run-coverage`: the host's `metrics coverage`
must report layout rule `v2` and valid observed/skipped accounting. Doctor
independently compares both eligible unique results and candidate-directory/
barrier counts against the Node production admission projection and layout scan.
Both read the main checkout store, including from a worktree. A candidate run
directory changed in the last 60 seconds permits a bounded transient difference,
even before a result exists; future mtimes are recent for clock skew. The host's
`recentRuns` remains result-file based. Diagnostic paths are sample candidates,
not verified host omissions. An unknown coverage subcommand or a response
without `layoutRule` identifies an old host positively and reports
passed-but-degraded with an upgrade instruction; other host errors fail.
This check is read-only, introduces no config default, and never rewrites runs.

`convention-conformance` checks the packaged naming and placement rules only
inside an fgOS source checkout. Violations on paths already present at the
rule cutoff pass with counts and up to three examples; a violation on a path
introduced after that cutoff fails the check, even while the rule posture is
`warn`. A missing or old host pass-skips with the reason because doctor never
reimplements the native rules. The check is read-only and has no registered
fix or config default.


`active-release-matches-checkout` compares a source checkout's Node payload
working-tree bytes with its own activated manifest, using the release builder's
source enumeration. It reports changed, missing and extra source files, excludes
staged production dependencies, and does not certify Rust host freshness.
Outside source checkouts, without activation, with a same-checkout development
manifest, or in a linked worktree whose activation belongs to main, it reports
a reasoned skip. Unsafe paths and unreadable inputs fail this check rather than
throwing out the whole doctor run. It is read-only, with no registered fix:
`npm run fgos:dev -- <verb>` runs working-tree code; build/stage/upgrade updates
plain `fgos`. Diagnosis never changes the activation implicitly.


| Check | Pass | Fail | Not applicable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `documentation-cutover-lease` | Repository hooks are wired, the committed main-ref sidecar is absent, released or abandoned, and no stray main token exists. | Committed sidecar is corrupt/unreadable; a token exists in main while main is not the recorded holder; applicable hook wiring is missing; or a lease is held. Held state reports age and frozen scope, or a missing hook/kernel lock resource. | Outside Git or without a main branch; also without `.githooks/reference-transaction` when authority is neither held nor corrupt and no stray main token exists. |

This check reads committed main-ref authority before treating missing repository hooks as not applicable: held/corrupt authority still fails if the reference hook disappears. It diagnoses a stray main token by file presence and the recorded holder checkout, without validating a linked holder's token possession. Acquire refuses the same stray condition with `stray-main-token`; held-lease admission also refuses main callers with that residue. The check is read-only, with no registered fix, config default or automatic token cleanup. After checking committed state and the recorded holder, the owner removes residue by hand; a real holder's release restores any pre-existing main token bytes. The [lease contract](../../holder-lock/spec.md#documentation-cutover-write-lease) owns the release crash window and recovery.

`fgos doctor --fix`:

- runs every registered fix;
- reports fix results;
- then reports checks.

## 4. Legacy Setup Compatibility

Current legacy `fgos setup` is deprecated but still reachable:

- wires known local support such as shell integration and hooks where applicable;
- ensures shared config defaults are present;
- runs every registered fix unconditionally;
- reports changes;
- preserves idempotency when run repeatedly.

The command registry and setup result payload expose the deprecation and workspace-onboarding path. This is implemented behavior, not the target architecture. New distribution design should route workspace onboarding through `fgctl init` plus local `fgos init`/`doctor --fix`/`doctor`, while preserving `fgos setup` as the legacy shell/global integration path through the 30-day preview fallback window unless a later release decision replaces that behavior. Removing the command entirely remains gated by that release-policy window, not by implementation-side inference.

## 5. Config Merge Contract

Config merge is fill-missing-only:

- customized values are not overwritten;
- nested object defaults fill missing keys;
- arrays are added wholesale only when missing;
- project config wins over global config for matching keys;
- missing global config is not an error.

## 6. Ownership Boundary

Doctor/fix paths may repair environment readiness. They must not silently select a different runtime identity when a workspace activation is present. Runtime selection belongs to `fgctl` and workspace activation records.

## 7. Implementation Evidence

| Claim | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Checks/fixes/defaults are registered through open registries | `src/setup/checks.mjs`, `src/setup/registrations.mjs`, `test/setup/registrations.test.mjs` |
| Doctor default path is read-only | `bin/fgos.mjs`, `test/setup/*.test.mjs` |
| Doctor fix runs registered fixes | `src/setup/registrations.mjs`, `bin/fgos.mjs`, `test/setup/*.test.mjs` |
| Legacy setup runs registered fixes and declares its deprecation path | `bin/fgos.mjs`, `src/cli/command-registry.mjs`, `docs/history/setup-runs-registered-fixes/CONTEXT.md`, `test/cli/fgos-manifest.test.mjs`, `test/setup/checks-setup-rc-line.test.mjs` |
| Project config overrides global config | `src/config/global-config.mjs`, `test/config/global-config.test.mjs` |

## 8. Open Follow-Up

The exact list of registered checks/fixes changes over time. This contract should avoid carrying a stale giant list; generated registry reports or verification docs should carry snapshots when needed.

##### Contributor hooks setup

- **Blocked when:** never — this is an explicit command a contributor runs
  themselves; it always runs when invoked.
- **What changes:** running the setup command wires up this repository's
  pre-commit hook for the person who just cloned it. It is never triggered
  automatically by any package manager's install step (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle)
  — a contributor runs it once, by hand, after cloning.
- **Side effects:** none beyond the local git config change; nothing is
  installed and no network access happens.
- **Afterwards:** the contributor's local clone has the pre-commit hook
  wired up, identically to what used to happen automatically. Someone who
  never runs this command simply does not get the local hook — this is a
  one-time manual step for contributors, not a requirement for installing
  or running `fgos` itself.

  its own allowlist, including linked worktrees and `fgw/*` branches. Existing
  root modifications/deletions remain permitted. Allowlist changes must land
  separately on main before root additions use them; the index cannot authorize
  itself. Merge commits skip only this root guard, never existing data-loss
  guards. `main-checkout-hook-wired` diagnoses wiring using the existing check.
- In fgOS source checkouts, the hook sends newly staged, copied, or renamed
  Markdown files directly under `plans/reports/` and `plans/journals/` to the
  native Convention checker. Violations and unavailable, old, or failed hosts
  emit warnings only; the hook never blocks the commit for Convention results.
  Nested evidence and per-plan `reports/` directories are outside this scope.

##### Setup

- **Blocked when:** never — running `fgos setup` always attempts its work;
  a shell profile that does not exist is simply skipped rather than
  refused.
- **What changes:** for every shell profile the caller actually has (bash's
  and/or zsh's, whichever exist), the shell helper's source line is added
  if not already present — never duplicated on a repeat run. The local
  project config file is also brought up to date: any setting present in
  the current default schema but missing from the caller's file is added,
  without ever changing a setting the caller already customized; a config
  file that already has every current default is left untouched. The same
  fill-missing-only treatment is applied to the **global** config file
  (`~/.fgos/config.json`, tsk-1ri) — `fgos setup` initializes it with the
  same default schema the project-local file gets, or fills in any missing
  key, every time it runs, regardless of which project it's run from;
  a value the caller already customized at the global level is never
  overwritten. The lock directories of row 5g are created when missing:
  `<lockRoot>` and `<fgosDir>/locks`, both mode 0700, an existing one tightened to it (the `lock-dirs` fix);
  the `terminal` section of row 5h is one of the defaults the
  fill-missing-only merge adds; `<stateRoot>/terminal` is created with mode 0700 (the
  `terminal-dir` fix).
- **Side effects:** the caller's own shell profile file(s), local project
  config file, global config file (`~/.fgos/config.json`), the two lock
  directories and `<stateRoot>/terminal` may be created or modified; nothing outside the caller's own
  environment is touched, and no network access happens.
- **Afterwards:** the caller sees exactly what changed — which profile
  file(s) gained the source line (or already had it), which project config
  settings were newly added (or that none were needed), and which global
  config settings were newly added (or that none were needed, or that the
  global file was just created). Nothing is done silently; running `fgos
  setup` again when everything is already current reports that plainly,
  without repeating any change.

##### Doctor

- **Blocked when:** never — `fgos doctor` always runs every check and
  reports the result; it never fails the invocation itself, only reports
  individual checks as passing or not. Exit stays 0 because `fgctl
  init|upgrade|repair` run it as their tail and mark the install degraded on
  a non-zero exit; `--strict` is the opt-in that exits 1 when any check fails.
- **What changes:** nothing — this is a read-only diagnostic. It never
  writes a config file, never modifies a shell profile, and never installs
  anything, even when a check reports a problem (`config-not-stale`
  failing on a missing config file reports that plainly rather than
  creating one).
- **Side effects:** none.
- **Afterwards:** the caller sees each named check (Data Dictionary #7) and
  whether it passed, including enough detail to know what to do next (e.g.
  which config settings are missing, or that `fgos setup` has not been run
  yet).

## 1. Purpose

The doctor/fix registry is the extension point for environment readiness. Modules register checks, fixes, and config defaults instead of adding one-off repair logic.

Target architecture has no separate `fgos setup` verb for workspace onboarding. `fgctl init` is the one-command workspace onboarding orchestrator; after activation it invokes active local `fgos init`, `fgos doctor --fix`, and `fgos doctor`. Legacy shell/global integration remains compatibility behavior under the explicit deprecated fallback window: 30 calendar days after preview release publication, unless a later release decision replaces that policy.

Current Node `fgos setup` remains implemented as deprecated legacy compatibility and consumes the same registry while it exists.

## 2. Registry Types

| Registry | Function | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Check | `registerCheck` | A named diagnostic reported by `fgos doctor`. |
| Fix | `registerFix` | A named repair run by `fgos doctor --fix`; current legacy `fgos setup` also runs fixes while it remains implemented. |
| Config default | `registerConfigDefault` | A default config shape merged into shared config without overwriting user values. |

`event-store` registers the `eventStore` config shape `{ remote: "origin" }`. Config merge fills missing keys while preserving explicit remote choices; the `git-repository-config` check diagnoses obsolete exact legacy mappings on the configured remote and on historical `origin`, and the `git-publication-refspecs` fix repairs them.

The registries are independent. A module may register only a check, only a fix, only a config default, or any combination.

## 3. Doctor Contract

`fgos doctor`:

- runs registered checks;
- reports individual pass/fail status as a row `{id, description, passed, message, detail?}`; `detail` is an optional JSON value that holds the facts behind the row's one-sentence `message` (for example the versions and floor behind a compatibility failure) and appears only in `fgos doctor --json`;
- does not write files by default;
- should tell the user what command or fix path applies when a check fails.

barrier counts against the Node production admission projection and layout scan.

without `layoutRule` identifies an old host positively and reports
passed-but-degraded with an upgrade instruction; other host errors fail.
This check is read-only, introduces no config default, and never rewrites runs.

`convention-conformance` checks the packaged naming and placement rules only

introduced after that cutoff fails the check, even while the rule posture is

reimplements the native rules. The check is read-only and has no registered
fix or config default.


`active-release-matches-checkout` compares a source checkout's Node payload

- reports fix results;
- then reports checks.

- wires known local support such as shell integration and hooks where applicable;
- ensures shared config defaults are present;
- runs every registered fix unconditionally;
- reports changes;
- preserves idempotency when run repeatedly.

The command registry and setup result payload expose the deprecation and workspace-onboarding path. This is implemented behavior, not the target architecture. New distribution design should route workspace onboarding through `fgctl init` plus local `fgos init`/`doctor --fix`/`doctor`, while preserving `fgos setup` as the legacy shell/global integration path through the 30-day preview fallback window unless a later release decision replaces that behavior. Removing the command entirely remains gated by that release-policy window, not by implementation-side inference.

## 5. Config Merge Contract

Config merge is fill-missing-only:

- customized values are not overwritten;
- nested object defaults fill missing keys;
- arrays are added wholesale only when missing;
- project config wins over global config for matching keys;
- missing global config is not an error.

## 6. Ownership Boundary

Doctor/fix paths may repair environment readiness. They must not silently select a different runtime identity when a workspace activation is present. Runtime selection belongs to `fgctl` and workspace activation records.

The durability line of `git-component-compatible` reports the process-crash/fsync contract without certifying stable media.

`git-repository-config` reports repository-local transport settings that Publication/Remote refuse, using Rust’s scope-based admission policy. For actions/checkout credentials, use `persist-credentials: false`, remove the repo-local `http.<url>.extraheader`, and configure a trusted global credential helper or `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`-level setting. Added in candidate — complete source units from `docs/specs/distribution.md` at blob `13d2e172de35a570d148022d4c859cac05223acb`, after the boundary main sync. Dated decisions, implementation rules and recorded gaps are retained; current assertions remain subject to the independent truth sample.

##### Contributor hooks setup

- **Blocked when:** never — this is an explicit command a contributor runs
  themselves; it always runs when invoked.
- **What changes:** running the setup command wires up this repository's
  pre-commit hook for the person who just cloned it. It is never triggered
  automatically by any package manager's install step (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle)
  — a contributor runs it once, by hand, after cloning.
- **Side effects:** none beyond the local git config change; nothing is
  installed and no network access happens.
- **Afterwards:** the contributor's local clone has the pre-commit hook
  wired up, identically to what used to happen automatically. Someone who
  never runs this command simply does not get the local hook — this is a
  one-time manual step for contributors, not a requirement for installing
  or running `fgos` itself.
- In fgOS source checkouts, the hook refuses newly staged root files outside
  its own allowlist, including linked worktrees and `fgw/*` branches. Existing
  root modifications/deletions remain permitted. Allowlist changes must land
  separately on main before root additions use them; the index cannot authorize
  itself. Merge commits skip only this root guard, never existing data-loss
  guards. `main-checkout-hook-wired` diagnoses wiring using the existing check.
- In fgOS source checkouts, the hook sends newly staged, copied, or renamed
  Markdown files directly under `plans/reports/` and `plans/journals/` to the
  native Convention checker. Violations and unavailable, old, or failed hosts
  emit warnings only; the hook never blocks the commit for Convention results.
  Nested evidence and per-plan `reports/` directories are outside this scope.

##### Setup

- **Blocked when:** never — running `fgos setup` always attempts its work;
  a shell profile that does not exist is simply skipped rather than
  refused.
- **What changes:** for every shell profile the caller actually has (bash's
  and/or zsh's, whichever exist), the shell helper's source line is added
  if not already present — never duplicated on a repeat run. The local
  project config file is also brought up to date: any setting present in
  the current default schema but missing from the caller's file is added,
  without ever changing a setting the caller already customized; a config
  file that already has every current default is left untouched. The same
  fill-missing-only treatment is applied to the **global** config file
  (`~/.fgos/config.json`, tsk-1ri) — `fgos setup` initializes it with the
  same default schema the project-local file gets, or fills in any missing
  key, every time it runs, regardless of which project it's run from;
  a value the caller already customized at the global level is never
  overwritten. The lock directories of row 5g are created when missing:
  `<lockRoot>` and `<fgosDir>/locks`, both mode 0700, an existing one tightened to it (the `lock-dirs` fix);
  the `terminal` section of row 5h is one of the defaults the
  fill-missing-only merge adds; `<stateRoot>/terminal` is created with mode 0700 (the
  `terminal-dir` fix).
- **Side effects:** the caller's own shell profile file(s), local project
  config file, global config file (`~/.fgos/config.json`), the two lock
  directories and `<stateRoot>/terminal` may be created or modified; nothing outside the caller's own
  environment is touched, and no network access happens.
- **Afterwards:** the caller sees exactly what changed — which profile
  file(s) gained the source line (or already had it), which project config
  settings were newly added (or that none were needed), and which global
  config settings were newly added (or that none were needed, or that the
  global file was just created). Nothing is done silently; running `fgos
  setup` again when everything is already current reports that plainly,
  without repeating any change.

##### Doctor

- **Blocked when:** never — `fgos doctor` always runs every check and
  reports the result; it never fails the invocation itself, only reports
  individual checks as passing or not. Exit stays 0 because `fgctl
  init|upgrade|repair` run it as their tail and mark the install degraded on
  a non-zero exit; `--strict` is the opt-in that exits 1 when any check fails.
- **What changes:** nothing — this is a read-only diagnostic. It never
  writes a config file, never modifies a shell profile, and never installs
  anything, even when a check reports a problem (`config-not-stale`
  failing on a missing config file reports that plainly rather than
  creating one).
- **Side effects:** none.
- **Afterwards:** the caller sees each named check (Data Dictionary #7) and
  whether it passed, including enough detail to know what to do next (e.g.
  which config settings are missing, or that `fgos setup` has not been run
  yet).
